title: A method for reading articles independently
text: Lesson overview Level B2 begins with a change of pace: from now on, you will read articles written in the style of pan-Arab newspapers, 300–400 words long, without vowel marks or simplified texts. The dictionary remains useful, but its role changes: it becomes your last resort, rather than your starting point. In this unit, you will learn a four-stage method (before reading, reading for gist, detailed reading and after reading), recognise genres in the Arabic press, locate the main verb in a long sentence, decide which words to look up, and use the framing expressions that connect a news item to its context ( ⁧عَلَى خَلْفِيَّةِ⁩ …, ⁧فِي إِطَارِ⁩ …, ⁧فِي ظِلِّ⁩ …). Three weeks, alongside EGY-11. Item Details Code B2-01 Level B2 · Module B2.1 News and institutions of the European Communities Prerequisites Examination B1 exceeded; B1-15 → B1-18 (titles, news, reading without vowels, news) and INT-01 (sources) Estimated time 18–20 hours · three weeks (weeks 157–159 of the calendar), plus the EGY track-11 in separate blocks Materials This unit, dictionary by root, chronometer, pencils of three colors, script for speech synthesis, sessions with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognizing the genres of the Arab press (news, service, investigation, interview, analysis, opinion article, editorial) and what to expect from each; 2. use the text's "seals" (section, title, subtitle, signature, place and date) to predict the content; 3. find main verb, subject and engraved in a period of 40–60 words; 4. decide which unknown words to seek, guess or ignore, and guess the meaning from the root, scheme and context; 5. understand the print-frame expressions and fill out a readsheet; 6. read in silence an article by 300 words at least 80 words per minute and summarize it in three sentences. Three-week plan. Dialogue 1 · Thirty words in the dictionary First day of the course B2. Salmā asks Luke how the holiday reading went: a true article in an Arabic newspaper. Arabic Translation ⁧كَيْفَ كَانَتْ تَجْرِبَتُكَ مَعَ الجَرِيدَةِ يَا لُوكَا؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: How was your experience with the newspaper, Luca? ⁧صَعْبَةٌ جِدًّا! قَرَأْتُ مَقَالًا عَنْ أَزْمَةِ المِيَاهِ، وَبَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ كُنْتُ مَا زِلْتُ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧فِي الفِقْرَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ.⁩ It's so hard! I read an article about the water crisis, and after an hour I was still in paragraph two. ⁧لِمَاذَا؟ مَاذَا فَعَلْتَ؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: Why? What did you do? ⁧كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ لَا أَعْرِفُهَا كُنْتُ أَبْحَثُ عَنْهَا فِي القَامُوسِ. وَجَدْتُ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧ثَلَاثِينَ كَلِمَةً جَدِيدَةً!⁩ Luke: Every word I didn't know I was looking for in the dictionary. I found 30 new words! ⁧هٰذَا هُوَ الخَطَأُ. فِي هٰذَا المُسْتَوَى، القَامُوسُ آخِرُ أَدَاةٍ، لَا أَوَّلُهَا.⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: Here's the mistake. At this level the dictionary is the last tool, not the first. ⁧فَكَيْفَ أَفْهَمُ إِذَنْ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luke: So how do I understand? ⁧العُنْوَانُ، وَالعُنْوَانُ الفَرْعِيُّ، وَاسْمُ⁩ : ⁧النَّصِّ⁩ « ⁧عَتَبَاتِ⁩ » ⁧اِبْدَأْ مِنْ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧الكَاتِبِ أَوِ الوَكَالَةِ، وَالتَّارِيخُ. ثُمَّ اقْرَأِ الفِقْرَةَ الأُولَى وَالفِقْرَةَ الأَخِيرَةَ.⁩ Salmā: Starts with the text's "soles": the title, subtitle, name of author or agency, date. Then read the first and last paragraphs. ⁧قَبْلَ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ المَقَالَ كُلَّهُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luke: Before reading the entire article? ⁧نَعَمْ. سَتَعْرِفُ عَمَّ يَتَحَدَّثُ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَبْدَأَ. ثُمَّ اقْرَأْهُ كَامِلًا مَرَّةً⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧وَاحِدَةً، دُونَ قَامُوسٍ، وَضَعْ خَطًّا تَحْتَ الأَفْعَالِ.⁩ Salmā: Yes. You'll know what he's talking about before you start. Then read it all once, without dictionary, and emphasize the verbs. ⁧تَحْتَ الأَفْعَالِ؟ لِمَاذَا؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ The verbs? Why? ⁧لِأَنَّ الفِعْلَ قَلْبُ الجُمْلَةِ. إِذَا عَرَفْتَ مَنْ فَعَلَ مَاذَا، فَهِمْتَ نِصْفَ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: Because the verb is the heart of the sentence. If you know who did what, you understand half of the ⁧الخَبَرِ.⁩ news. Arabic Translation ⁧وَالكَلِمَاتُ الجَدِيدَةُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luke: What about the new words? ⁧اِسْأَلْ نَفْسَكَ ثَلَاثَةَ أَسْئِلَةٍ: هَلْ تَتَكَرَّرُ الكَلِمَةُ؟ هَلْ هِيَ فِي⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧، فَتَجَاوَزْهَا.⁩ « ⁧لَا⁩ » ⁧العُنْوَانِ؟ هَلْ يَتَوَقَّفُ عَلَيْهَا المَعْنَى؟ إِذَا كَانَ الجَوَابُ⁩ Salmā: Ask yourself three questions: does the word repeat itself? Is it in the title? Does the sense depend on you? If the answer is "no" then skip it. ⁧يَعْنِي أَقْبَلُ أَلَّا أَفْهَمَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luca: I mean, do I agree not to understand everything? ⁧بِالضَّبْطِ. القَارِئُ الجَيِّدُ لَا يَفْهَمُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ، بَلْ يَفْهَمُ النَّصَّ.⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: Exactly. The good reader does not understand every word: he understands the text. What to notice. ⁧مَا زِلْتُ⁩ I was still in the middle of it.A2-07). ⁧آخِرُ أَدَاةٍ، لَا أَوَّلُهَا⁩ The last instrument, not the first instrument: ⁧أَدَاة⁩ Tool: ⁧عَتَبَات⁩ pl. of ⁧عَتَبَة⁩ In Arabic literary criticism ⁧عَتَبَاتُ النَّصِّ⁩ " are title, subtitle, author, preface. ⁧عَمَّ⁩ = ⁧عَنْ⁩ + ⁧مَا⁩ . ⁧ضَعْ خَطًّا تَحْتَ⁩ • underlines (Lett. "Put a line under the heading "). ⁧يَتَوَقَّفُ عَلَى⁩ It is dependent on the product (s). ⁧تَجَاوَزْ⁩ the need to ⁧تَجَاوَزَ⁩ • Pass, skip. ⁧أَلَّا⁩ = ⁧أَنْ⁩ + ⁧لَا⁩ . 2. The genres of the Arab press Every genre has a different structure and voice: knowing what you are reading tells you where to look for facts and where opinions. Genre Arabic What it contains Where to look news ⁧خَبَر⁩ essential facts, with the source the first paragraph service, reportage ⁧تَقْرِير⁩ facts, voices, numbers, context first paragraph + quotations investigation ⁧تَحْقِيق⁩ research of the journalist: testimonials, data, documents Introduction and conclusion interview ⁧مُقَابَلَة⁩ · ⁧حِوَار⁩ questions and answers questions: say the themes analysis ⁧تَحْلِيل⁩ causes, consequences, scenarios; expert voices sentences with ⁧يَرَى⁩ , ⁧يُرَجَّحُ⁩ , ⁧مِنَ⁩ ⁧المُتَوَقَّعِ⁩ Rule of opinion, heading · ⁧مَقَالُ رَأْيٍ⁩ ⁧عَمُود⁩ the thesis of a signed author the last paragraph editorial ⁧اِفْتِتَاحِيَّة⁩ the opinion of the headboard, usually not signed the tone and conclusion Facts and opinions. In the news and in the service, the journalist does not say "I": opinions are attributed ( ⁧قَالَ⁩ , ⁧أَكَّدَ⁩ , ⁧رَأَى⁩ ). In the opinion article and editorial, the opinion is of the author, often in first person or with formulas such as ⁧فِي تَقْدِيرِي⁩ , ⁧لَا شَكَّ أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧مِنَ الوَاضِحِ أَنَّ⁩ . The module B2.2 will come back to this in detail (B2-12). 3. Before reading, write in English two lines:          ♪ I think the article speaks of... I expect to find... (numbers, statements, criticisms) ♪ After reading check: even a wrong prediction made you read carefully. The signature. «( ⁧وَكَالَات⁩ ) (i) means that the text is built on agency dispatches; « ⁧عَمَّانُ⁩ – ⁧مُرَاسِلُنَا⁩ • that there is a correspondent on the spot; a name and a surname after ⁧كَتَبَ⁩ or ⁧كَتَبَتْ⁩ , that there is a responsible author. For the review of sources (INT-01) is information to be noted. 4. Global Reading and Selective Reading Global reading (to understand what it is, 2–3 minutes): title and subtitle → first full paragraph → first sentence of each paragraph → last paragraph. Meanwhile, it circles: own names, numbers, words that repeat themselves. In the end write a sentence: "The article speaks of... and claims / reports that... Selective reading (to find precise information): you already know what you are looking for (a date, a digit, the name of the person who said a sentence) and scroll the text with your eyes only for that, without reading the rest. It is the reading you use for a press review or to answer specific questions. Analytical reading (to understand everything): paragraph by paragraph, with the three pencils. Red for the main verbs, blue for the sources (who says), green for the connectives and the expressions-frame. Just at this point, and only for the decisive words, open the dictionary. 5. The Long Period In the Arab press a period of 50 words with a single comma is not uncommon. The secret is to find the dorsal puppy: main verb, subject, complement. Everything else is hanging from her. ⁧وأعلن وزير الموارد المائية، في مؤتمر صحفي عقده أمس على هامش اجتماع وزراء المياه العرب في⁩ ⁧عمان، أن بلاده ستطلق خلال الأشهر المقبلة مشروعا لتحلية مياه البحر، بتمويل من صندوق إقليمي، يهدف⁩ ⁧إلى تأمين مياه الشرب لأكثر من مليوني نسمة.⁩ ⁧المَوَارِدُ المَائِيَّةُ⁩ Water resources ⁧تَحْلِيَة⁩ Desalting · ⁧تَأْمِين⁩ • to ensure • • ⁧نَسَمَة⁩ (in the accounts). Over What are you looking for? Over the period 1 the first verb conjugated outside the engravings ⁧أَعْلَنَ⁩ 2 the subject (immediately after, in the verbal sentence) ⁧وَزِيرُ المَوَارِدِ المَائِيَّةِ⁩ Over What are you looking for? Over the period 3 the engraved, between commas, introduced by prepositions … ⁧فِي مُؤْتَمَرٍ صَحَفِيٍّ عَقَدَهُ أَمْسِ عَلَى هَامِشِ⁩ 4 the complement: here is a phrase with ⁧أَنَّ بِلَادَهُ سَتُطْلِقُأَنَّ⁩ ⁧مَشْرُوعًا⁩ … 5 complements … ⁧بِتَمْوِيلٍ مِنْ⁩ · ⁧لِتَحْلِيَةِ مِيَاهِ البَحْرِ⁩ · ⁧خِلَالَ الأَشْهُرِ المُقْبِلَةِ⁩ 6 descriptive phrases (sifa) without relative pronoun ( ⁧مَشْرُوعًا⁩ reported a) … ⁧يَهْدِفُ إِلَى تَأْمِينِ⁩ The spine: ⁧أَعْلَنَ الوَزِيرُ أَنَّ بِلَادَهُ سَتُطْلِقُ مَشْرُوعًا⁩ The Minister announced that his country would launch a project. The rest responds to where? When? for what? With what money? for what purpose? The syntax of the long period (chains of iḍāfa, relative without pronoun) is the argument of B2-02. Useful clues. The Arabic comma ( ⁧،⁩ ) often separates an engraving; ⁧وَ⁩ at the beginning of a period does not mean "and" but marks only the beginning of a new paragraph or of a new information; ⁧كَمَا⁩ , ⁧فِيمَا⁩ , ⁧بَيْنَمَا⁩ open parallel information. 6. Dialogue 2 · The reversed pyramid Video call between Luca and Laylā Ḥaddād, the Beirut journalist. Arabic Translation ⁧لَيْلَى، أَنْتِ صَحَفِيَّةٌ مُنْذُ عِشْرِينَ سَنَةً. كَيْفَ تَكْتُبِينَ خَبَرًا؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luca: LaylāYou've been a journalist for 20 years. How do you write news? ⁧الأَهَمُّ أَوَّلًا. فِي الفِقْرَةِ الأُولَى⁩ :« ⁧الهَرَمِ المَقْلُوبِ⁩ » ⁧نَكْتُبُ بِطَرِيقَةِ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧نُجِيبُ عَنِ الأَسْئِلَةِ الأَسَاسِيَّةِ: مَنْ؟ مَاذَا؟ مَتَى؟ أَيْنَ؟⁩ Laylā: We write with the reversed pyramid: first the most important thing. In the first paragraph we answer the fundamental questions: who? What? When? Where? ⁧وَكَيْفَ؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ How? Why? ⁧تَأْتِي بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ، فِي الفِقْرَاتِ التَّالِيَةِ، مَعَ التَّصْرِيحَاتِ وَرُدُودِ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧الفِعْلِ.⁩ Laylā: They come after, in the following paragraphs, with statements and reactions. ⁧وَمَا الَّذِي يَأْتِي فِي النِّهَايَةِ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luke: And what comes to the end? ⁧تَارِيخُ القَضِيَّةِ، أَرْقَامٌ سَابِقَةٌ، أَحْدَاثٌ مُشَابِهَةٌ. وَغَالِبًا⁩ : ⁧الخَلْفِيَّةُ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ .«… ⁧قَدْ⁩ … ⁧وَكَانَتْ⁩ » ⁧أَوْ⁩ « ⁧يُذْكَرُ أَنَّ⁩ » ⁧تَبْدَأُ بِعِبَارَاتٍ مِثْلِ⁩ Laylā: The context: the history of the question, previous numbers, similar facts. And it often begins with expressions like ... ..you remember that he had.......................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................... ⁧آه، لِهٰذَا السَّبَبِ الفِقْرَةُ الأَخِيرَةُ صَعْبَةٌ دَائِمًا! فِيهَا أَفْعَالٌ فِي⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧المَاضِي البَعِيدِ.⁩ Luke: Ah, that's why the last paragraph is always difficult! There are verbs at the passageway. ⁧هٰذَا مَاضٍ قَبْلَ⁩ :«… ⁧وَكَانَتِ الحُكُومَةُ قَدْ أَعْلَنَتْ⁩ » ⁧صَحِيحٌ.⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ :« ⁧فِي إِطَارِ⁩ » ⁧وَ⁩ « ⁧عَلَى خَلْفِيَّةِ⁩ » ⁧المَاضِي. وَانْتَبِهْ أَيْضًا إِلَى عِبَارَاتٍ مِثْلِ⁩ ⁧هِيَ الَّتِي تَرْبِطُ الخَبَرَ بِسِيَاقِهِ.⁩ Laylā: Right. The government had announced... ... that it is a past before the past. And also be careful with expressions like ⁧وَفِي مَقَالَاتِ الرَّأْيِ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luke: And in the articles of opinion? Arabic Translation ⁧هُنَاكَ القَاعِدَةُ مُخْتَلِفَةٌ: الكَاتِبُ يَبْدَأُ بِفِكْرَةٍ أَوْ بِسُؤَالٍ، وَيَتْرُكُ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧رَأْيَهُ لِلنِّهَايَةِ أَحْيَانًا. لِذٰلِكَ لَا تَحْكُمْ عَلَى مَقَالِ رَأْيٍ مِنْ فِقْرَتِهِ الأُولَى.⁩ Laylā: There the rule is different: the author begins with an idea or a question, and sometimes leaves his opinion for the end. Therefore do not judge an article of opinion from the first paragraph. ⁧سَأُحَاوِلُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ الصُّحُفَ العَرَبِيَّةَ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luke: I'll try to read Arabic newspapers every morning. ⁧كُلَّ⁩ : ⁧اِبْدَأْ بِالأَخْبَارِ القَصِيرَةِ، ثُمَّ التَّقَارِيرِ، ثُمَّ الاِفْتِتَاحِيَّاتِ. وَالأَهَمُّ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧يَوْمٍ، وَلَوْ رُبْعَ سَاعَةٍ.⁩ Laylā: Start with short news, then services, then editorials. And above all: every day, even for 15 minutes. What to notice. ⁧الهَرَمُ المَقْلُوبُ⁩ The pyramid is reversed: the structure of the news in all languages. ⁧رُدُودُ الفِعْلِ⁩ • the reactions (pl. of ⁧رَدُّ فِعْلٍ⁩ ). ⁧مُشَابِه⁩ • similar • similar. ⁧كَانَ⁩ … ⁧قَدْ⁩ + Perfect = Passed (A2-20): ⁧وَكَانَتِ الحُكُومَةُ قَدْ أَعْلَنَتْ⁩ The government had announced that it would not be able to do so. ⁧لَا تَحْكُمْ عَلَى⁩ Do not judge. ⁧وَلَوْ⁩ It's even just a little bit. 7. The Words You Don't Know Looking, guessing or ignoring? Question If so If not Is it in the title, subtitle or first sentence? If you can't guess it, look for it. continue with the question after Do you repeat it two or more times? Probably a keyword: guess it or find it continue Without her the phrase loses sense (it is the verb guess it; If you can't, look for it ignore it and go ahead main, subject)? Guess in four steps. 1. Isolate root (G)41). 2. Recognize the scheme: maṣdar, participle, place name, derivative form (G42–G47). 3. Combine the meaning of the root and the pattern. 4. Check in context: your hypothesis must work in the sentence. Word Root + scheme Hypothesis In context ⁧ر ش دتَرْشِيد⁩ Driving, common sense + maṣdar II ⁧ر ش دتَرْشِيد⁩ • make rational • make rational • make rational ⁧تَرْشِيدُ الاِسْتِهْلَاكِ⁩ • rationalising consumption ⁧و س عتَوْسِيع⁩ • wide • + maṣdar II ⁧و س عتَوْسِيع⁩ Expanding ⁧تَوْسِيعُ المِينَاءِ⁩ Port enlargement ⁧ع ق داِنْعِقَاد⁩ ⁧ع ق داِنْعِقَاد⁩ Legare, hold (one meeting) . maṣdar VII • to unfold ⁧اِنْعِقَادُ القِمَّةِ⁩ The summit will take place at the end of this year. ⁧ض ر رمُتَضَرِّر⁩ • damage • + participle V The person who has suffered damage shall: ⁧الأُسَرُ المُتَضَرِّرَةُ⁩ • damaged households • damaged households • damaged households ⁧ز ي دمُتَزَايِد⁩ Increased + Participle VI ⁧طَلَبٌ مُتَزَايِدٌ⁩ A growing demand is likely to increase. The limits of guessing. Oral production 1. Present an article (session). Bring the tutor a real article read in the week (Appendix C). In three minutes present it in Arabic: testata, genre, argumenta, eventi principali, fonti, contexto. Use at least two frame expressions. 2. The review. As in Script B, it presents in one and a half minutes three articles (even short) of the same day, with formulas ⁧أَمَّا صَحِيفَةُ⁩ … ⁧فَـ⁩ … · ⁧وَفِي صَحِيفَةِ⁩ … · ⁧خَصَّصَتْ⁩ … · ⁧نَشَرَتْ⁩ …. 3. The method. Explains to an imaginary companion, in Arabic, how to read an article without getting lost in the dictionary (the four steps and the three questions). 19. Typical errors Error Correction search every new word as soon as you meet it first global reading without dictionary; then only the decisive words take the first name after the verb as a complement in the verbal sentence the subject comes immediately after the verb Getting lost in the engraved delimites the engraved in brackets and finds the spine translating ⁧وَ⁩ Initial with at the beginning of the period often does not translate translating always ⁧عَلَى خَلْفِيَّةِ⁩ with ... on the background of ... it often means "by" following, by" exchanging an opinion article for a news report look at the thresholds (sign, section) and opinion markers read ⁧كَانَتْ⁩ … ⁧قَدْ أَعْلَنَتْ⁩ as a simple past is a transgressor: "He had announced" 20. Active booster review Cover the right column, answer aloud, then check. Question Answer The four stages of reading Before reading · global reading · analytical reading · after reading (sheet) The three questions about the new words Do you repeat yourself? Is it in the title? Does the sense depend on you? editorial · survey · analysis ⁧تَحْلِيل⁩ · ⁧تَحْقِيق⁩ · ⁧اِفْتِتَاحِيَّة⁩ • Subtitles: • Paragraph: ⁧فِقْرَة⁩ · ⁧عُنْوَانٌ فَرْعِيٌّ⁩ In the context of the ... ⁧عَلَى هَامِشِ⁩ · ⁧فِي إِطَارِ⁩ In the light of the provisions of this Regulation, the following definitions shall apply: ⁧فِي ظِلِّ⁩ · ⁧فِي ضَوْءِ⁩ (Case) ⁧عَلَى خَلْفِيَّةِ⁩ • highlight the theme of the project ⁧تَطَرَّقَ إِلَى⁩ · ⁧سَلَّطَ الضَّوْءَ عَلَى⁩ The latest developments in the dossier are: ⁧آخِرُ مُسْتَجَدَّاتِ المِلَفِّ⁩ • had announced • (she) ⁧كَانَتْ قَدْ أَعْلَنَتْ⁩ Speed target now · at end B2 80 · 90 words per minute 21. Unit verification Twenty points; Exceeding at least 16. The text (invented news). ⁧مجتمع⁩ ⁧البلدية تطلق برنامجا لترميم المدارس القديمة⁩ « ⁧لن يبقى طالب في صف بلا تدفئة⁩ » ⁧الرئيس:⁩ ⁧مراسلنا⁩ – ⁧الإسكندرية⁩ ⁧أطلقت بلدية الإسكندرية أمس، في إطار خطة لتحسين البنية التحتية التعليمية، برنامجا لترميم ستين⁩ ⁧مدرسة يعود بناء معظمها إلى أكثر من نصف قرن، بتمويل مشترك من الحكومة وعدد من الشركات المحلية.⁩ ⁧وقال رئيس البلدية، في مؤتمر صحفي عقده على هامش زيارة لإحدى المدارس، إن الأعمال ستبدأ في⁩ ⁧الصيف المقبل، حتى لا تؤثر في الدراسة. وجاء الإعلان على خلفية شكاوى متكررة من أولياء الأمور بشأن⁩ ⁧حالة المباني. وكانت البلدية قد رممت عشرين مدرسة العام الماضي.⁩ ⁧البِنْيَةُ التَّحْتِيَّةُ⁩ • infrastructure • ⁧تَدْفِئَة⁩ Heating ⁧أَوْلِيَاءُ الأُمُورِ⁩ • parents (of pupils) • A · Analysis (8 points, 2 ). 1. Genre and thresholds: of what kind is the text, who writes, from where? What does the subtitle say? · 2. In the first period, write in Arabic the spine (verb, subject, complement) and indicate two incisions. · 3. Translate into context ⁧في إطار⁩ , ⁧على هامش⁩ and ⁧على خلفية.⁩ · 4. What does the last sentence say, and with what verbal time? Why does the reporter end up with it? B - Vocabulary (6 points). Write in Arabic: 5. Editorial · 6. in the light of · 7. the latest developments · 8. recommendation · 9. Translate: ⁧يسلط المقال الضوء على المشكلة.⁩ · 10. Translate: ⁧تطرق الوزير إلى ملف الهجرة.⁩ C - Summary (6 points). Write in Arabic the summary of the news in three sentences (subject and facts; reason; context). Evaluation: content (3 points) and form (3 points: neutrality, correctness, an expression-frame). 22. In B2-02 enter into the syntax of long periods: chains of iḍāfa, relative without pronouns, descriptive phrases and engraved, tools to disassemble any period of newspaper.

title: Advanced syntax: long periods, chains of iḍāfa, relative without pronoun
text: Lesson overview In B2-01 you have learned to find the dorsal spine of a long period. Now unmount the pieces that surround it: the chains of iḍāfa ( ⁧رَئِيسُ مَجْلِسِ إِدَارَةِ الشَّرِكَةِ⁩ ), adjectives referring to a distant element of the chain, descriptive phrases without relative pronoun ( ⁧مَشْرُوعًا يَهْدِفُ إِلَى⁩ ...), the parties acting as relative ( ⁧الدُّوَلُ المُشَارِكَةُ فِي المُؤْتَمَرِ⁩ , ⁧المَشْرُوعُ المُقَرَّرُ إِطْلَاقُهُ⁩ ), the relative nouns with ⁧مَا⁩ and ⁧مَنْ⁩ , the series of maṣdar co-ordinates and phrases with the predicate ( ⁧وَمِنَ المُقَرَّرِ أَنْ⁩ …). In the end, you can unpack a period of paper into simple sentences and rebuild it in a natural Italian. Four weeks, in parallel with EGY-11 and EGY-12. Item Details Code B2-02 Level B2 · Module B2.1 News and institutions of the European Communities Prerequisites B2-01; A2-09 (iḍāfa), A2-13 (relatives), B1-03 (participants), B1-04 (maṣdar) Estimated time 22–24 hours · four weeks (weeks 160–163), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, pencils of three colors, Grammar reference (G28, G32, G43, G44), voice synthesis scripts, tutor sessions Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. Read and build chains of iḍāfa of three or four terms, with the adjective in place and in the right case; 2. recognizing descriptive phrases without relative pronoun after an indeterminate name, and translating them with a relative to Italy; 3. understand the parts used as relative, including constructions ⁧المُقَرَّرُ⁩ + maṣdar + pronoun (s) expected which... 4. read the relevant nouns ( ⁧مَا قَالَهُ⁩ , ⁧مَنْ يُرِيدُ⁩ , ⁧مِمَّا⁩ ) and sentences with the predicate anticipated; 5. remove a period of 50–70 simple words and reconstruct them in English; 6. read an article by 330 words at least 80 words per minute. Four-week plan. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 2: the chain of iḍāfa 2 Section 3: the adjective at the bottom of the chain · exercise 1 3 Exercise 2 · lexicon (first part) 4 Section 4: descriptive phrases without pronoun · exercise 3 5 Script B · examples in context 6 Session with the tutor (oral production) 1) 7 Review of the week · reading 1 global 8 Section 5: the parties as related 9 Exercise 4 · lexicon (second part) 10 Section 6: the relevant nouns · exercise 5 Day Activity 11 Dialogue 2 · section 7: the predicate anticipated 12 Exercise 6 13 Reading 1 analytical · exercise 9 (a) 14 Session with the tutor (oral production) 2) 15 Section 8: disassemble and rebuild · exercise 7 16 Exercise 8 · Script C 17 Reading 2 timed · exercise 9 (b–c) 18 Translation (year 10) 19 Pronunciation · Script A 20 Session with the tutor (oral production) 3) 21 Writing (year 11), first version 22 Writing: review · exercise 12 23 General review · Active recall review 24 Unit verification 1. Dialogue 1 · The new president or the new council? Salmā wrote a newspaper headline on the board. Arabic Translation .« ⁧اِسْتِقَالَةُ رَئِيسِ مَجْلِسِ إِدَارَةِ الشَّرِكَةِ الجَدِيدِ⁩ » ⁧اِقْرَأْ يَا لُوكَا:⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: Read, Luke: • Resignation of the new president of the board of directors of the company. ⁧الجَدِيدُ هُوَ الشَّرِكَةُ؟⁩ … ⁧أَرْبَعُ كَلِمَاتٍ مُتَّصِلَةٌ ثُمَّ صِفَةٌ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luke: Four words tied and then an adjective... Is the new society? ⁧لَا يُمْكِنُ: الشَّرِكَةُ مُؤَنَّثَةٌ، وَالصِّفَةُ مُذَكَّرَةٌ.⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: Can't be: "society" is female and the adjective is male. ⁧إِذَنْ الإِدَارَةُ؟ لَا، هِيَ مُؤَنَّثَةٌ أَيْضًا. المَجْلِسُ أَوِ الرَّئِيسُ.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luca: So the administration? No, she's feminine too. The Council or the President. ⁧أَحْسَنْتَ. وَكَيْفَ تَخْتَارُ بَيْنَهُمَا؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: Bravo. And how do you choose between the two? ⁧بِالضَّمَّةِ⁩ « ⁧الجَدِيدُ⁩ » ⁧بِالكَسْرَةِ لِلْمَجْلِسِ، وَ⁩ « ⁧الجَدِيدِ⁩ » ⁧بِالحَرَكَاتِ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧لٰكِنْ فِي الجَرِيدَةِ لَا حَرَكَاتِ!⁩ … ⁧لِلرَّئِيسِ⁩ With vowels? «al-ǧadīdiWith the kasra for the council,al-ǧadīduThe ḍamma For the president... but there are no vowels in the paper! ⁧صَحِيحٌ. هُنَا يُسَاعِدُكَ المَعْنَى: الَّذِي يَسْتَقِيلُ شَخْصٌ، لَا⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧مَجْلِسٌ. فَالجَدِيدُ هُوَ الرَّئِيسُ.⁩ Salmā: Right. Here helps you the way: the person resigning is a person, not advice. So the new one is the president. ⁧وَإِذَا كَانَ المَعْنَى غَيْرَ وَاضِحٍ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luke: What if the meaning is not clear? ⁧اِسْتِقَالَةُ الرَّئِيسِ⁩ » ⁧الصَّحَفِيُّ الجَيِّدُ يُعِيدُ صِيَاغَةَ الجُمْلَةِ:⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: The good journalist rephrases the phrase: "al- raʾīs al-ǧadīd li-maǧlis…». With the lām the chain yes ⁧بِاللَّامِ تَنْكَسِرُ السِّلْسِلَةُ وَيَزُولُ⁩ .« ⁧الجَدِيدِ لِمَجْلِسِ إِدَارَةِ الشَّرِكَةِ⁩ breaks and ambiguity disappears. ⁧الغُمُوضُ.⁩ Arabic Translation ⁧السِّلْسِلَةُ طَوِيلَةٌ، وَالصِّفَةُ تَنْتَظِرُ فِي آخِرِهَا.⁩ : ⁧فَهِمْتُ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luca: I understand: the chain is long and the adjective waits at the bottom. ⁧بِالضَّبْطِ. لِأَنَّ لَا شَيْءَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَ المُضَافِ وَالمُضَافِ إِلَيْهِ. وَهٰذَا⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: Exactly. Because nothing can separate the first term of theiḍāfa The second. And that's it. ⁧مَا سَنَدْرُسُهُ اليَوْمَ.⁩ that we study today. What to notice. ⁧مُتَّصِلَة⁩ • Tie it up. ⁧أَحْسَنْتَ⁩ - Good boy! ⁧الحَرَكَات⁩ The short vowels are marked. ⁧يُعِيدُ صِيَاغَةَ⁩ Rewording (B1-21). ⁧تَنْكَسِرُ السِّلْسِلَةُ⁩ The chain breaks. ⁧يَزُولُ الغُمُوضُ⁩ The ambiguity disappears. ⁧لَا شَيْءَ يَفْصِلُ⁩ "Nothing separates" ⁧المُضَاف⁩ · ⁧المُضَاف إِلَيْهِ⁩ The first and second term of theiḍāfa». 2. The chain of iḍāfa Each term shall be the second of the preceding and the first of the following. The Rules of A2-09 They're valid for the whole chain. Rule Example Translation only the last term may have the article ⁧وَزِيرُ خَارِجِيَّةِ الدَّوْلَةِ⁩ the Minister for Foreign Affairs of the State All terms except the first one are at the genitive ⁧رَئِيسِ مَجْلِسِ النُّوَّابِ⁩ (after a preposition: also the first)  the chain is determined if the last term is ⁧مُدِيرُ مَكْتَبِ الوَزِيرِ⁩ The Director of the Minister's Office  indeterminate if the last is not ⁧مُدِيرُ مَكْتَبِ وَزِيرٍ⁩ The Director of a Minister's Office  the dual and the plural healthy lose the ⁧وَزِيرَا خَارِجِيَّةِ البَلَدَيْنِن⁩ ⁧مُوَظَّفُو وِزَارَةِ⁩ · ⁧المَالِيَّةِ⁩ the two foreign ministers · the employees of the Ministry of Finance a name with suffix closes the chain ⁧مُدِيرُ مَكْتَبِهِ⁩ the Director of his office Two first terms for one second. The norm wants the second term after the first and a pronoun after the second: ⁧مُدِيرُ المَدْرَسَةِ وَمُدَرِّسُوهَا⁩ The Director and teachers of the school are: Printing often also uses the form "contracted" ⁧مُدِيرُ وَمُدَرِّسُو المَدْرَسَةِ⁩ : Recognize her. ⁧غَيْر⁩ and ⁧شِبْه⁩ . They act like first words: ⁧غَيْرُ رَسْمِيٍّ⁩ Unofficial: ⁧غَيْرُ مَسْبُوقٍ⁩ Unprecedented, ⁧شِبْهُ جَزِيرَةٍ⁩ • Peninsula • Peninsula • Peninsula • Peninsula • Peninsula ⁧شِبْهُ يَوْمِيٍّ⁩ Almost daily. 3. The adjective at the bottom of the chain Nothing fits into the terms of aiḍāfa: therefore all adjectives go after the last term, even when they refer to the first. To understand the name an adjective uses in this order: Show Example What it refers to gender and number ⁧سِيَارَةُ مُدِيرِ الشَّرِكَةِ الجَدِيدَةُ⁩ New: ⁧سَيَّارَة⁩ or ⁧الشَّرِكَة⁩ (females), not ⁧مُدِير⁩ determination ⁧مَشْرُوعُ قَانُونٍ جَدِيدٌ⁩ New indeterminate: ⁧مَشْرُوع⁩ (the chain is indefinite) or ⁧قَانُون⁩ Show Example What it refers to chance, if there are vowels ⁧رَئِيسُ الوُزَرَاءِ الجَدِيدُ⁩ (name) the President sense ⁧اِسْتِقَالَةُ رَئِيسِ المَجْلِسِ⁩ ⁧الجَدِيدِ⁩ The one who resigns is the president order, if more ⁧وَزِيرُ الخَارِجِيَّةِ الإِيطَالِيُّ⁩ the adjective closest to his name comes before:         • the former Italian foreign minister adjectives ⁧السَّابِقُ⁩ Break the chain with ⁧لِـ⁩ . When ambiguity is real, the press uses ⁧لِـ⁩ : ⁧الرَّئِيسُ الجَدِيدُ لِلشَّرِكَةِ⁩ The new president of the company is hereby appointed. ⁧الاِجْتِمَاعُ السَّنَوِيُّ لِوُزَرَاءِ المِيَاهِ⁩ The annual meeting of water ministers is held. It is also the way to put an adjective immediately after the first name. 4. Descriptive phrases without relative pronoun After an indeterminate name its does not ⁧الَّذِي⁩ : the phrase follows directly the name (it is called ⁧جُمْلَةُ الصِّفَةِ⁩ ). It almost always contains a pronoun that refers to the name (the return pronoun) ⁧الضَّمِيرُ العَائِدُ⁩ ), except when the name is the subject of the verb. Background Descriptive phrase Translation  ⁧يَهْدِفُ إِلَى تَأْمِينِ المِيَاهِمَشْرُوعًا⁩ a project aimed at ensuring water  ⁧نَشَرَتْهُ الصَّحِيفَةُ أَمْسِتَقْرِيرٌ⁩ a report that the newspaper published yesterday  ⁧يَعِيشُ فِيهَا مِلْيُونُ نَسَمَةٍمَدِينَةٌ⁩ a city in which one million inhabitants live  ⁧يَمْلِكُهَا رَجُلُ أَعْمَالٍشَرِكَةٌ⁩ a company owned by an entrepreneur  ⁧لَمْ تَرَ النُّورَ بَعْدُخُطَّةٌ⁩ a plan that has not yet seen the light ⁧أَسْئِلَةٌ⁩ ⁧لَا جَوَابَ لَهَا⁩ unanswered questions The return pronoun says the function of the name in its: ⁧ـهُ⁩ / ⁧ـهَا⁩ object ( ⁧نَشَرَتْهُ⁩ ), ⁧فِيهَا⁩ "Where' means: ⁧لَهَا⁩ • which have been classified as having been classified in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation; ⁧مِنْهُ⁩ From which the value of the products used does not exceed 50% of the ex-works price of the product ⁧عَنْهَا⁩ Of which: In Italian, it translates with "che," in which, of which, from which it is. Attention: whether determined or not? ⁧مَشْرُوعٌ يَهْدِفُ⁩ ... (without ⁧الَّذِي⁩ ) ↔ ⁧المَشْرُوعُ الَّذِي يَهْدِفُ⁩ ... ( ⁧الَّذِي⁩ ). If you see a verb immediately after an indeterminate name, ask yourself if the phrase describes it: often yes. 5. Participants as related Active or passive participle with article = relative: ⁧الدُّوَلُ المُشَارِكَةُ فِي المُؤْتَمَرِ⁩ The countries participating in the conference are: ⁧الأُسَرُ المُتَضَرِّرَةُ⁩ • the damaged households • the damaged households • the damaged households • the damaged households • the damaged families • the damaged households • the damaged households • the damaged households • the damaged households • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • the damaged families • families • the damaged families • families • families • the damaged families • families • families • the damaged families • families • families • families • families • families • families • families • families • families • families • families • families • families • families • families • families • families • families ⁧القَرَارُ الصَّادِرُ أَمْسِ⁩ The decision given yesterday is the case. The passive participle construction + maṣdar + pronoun. Frequent in the press, it has no direct equivalent in English: Arabic literally. In Italian ⁧المَشْرُوعُ المُقَرَّرُ إِطْلَاقُهُ فِي الرَّبِيعِ⁩ the project established its launch in spring the project to be launched in spring Arabic literally. In Italian ⁧القِمَّةُ المُزْمَعُ عَقْدُهَا الشَّهْرَ المُقْبِلَ⁩ the summit decided to take place next month the summit planned for next month ⁧الوَفْدُ المُتَوَقَّعُ وُصُولُهُ غَدًا⁩ the delegation awaited its arrival tomorrow the delegation expected for tomorrow ⁧الاِنْتِخَابَاتُ المُقَرَّرُ إِجْرَاؤُهَا فِي⁩ ⁧الخَرِيفِ⁩ elections scheduled to take place in the autumn elections scheduled for autumn As you read. title: Political and institutional lexicon
text: Lesson overview INT-02 you have learned the names of institutions; in B1-16 The first vocabulary of the political chronicle. Now you enter political life as the newspapers tell: elections (campagna, turnout, strip, seats, ballots), governments (task, formation, coalition, reshuffle, distrust, resignation), parties and currents, referendums and constitutional reforms, the language of political crises and the passage of powers. You also learn to recognize regional variants of office names and procedures, and report results and percentages without errors. All the countries, parties and politicians of the texts are invented. Four weeks, in parallel with EGY-12. Item Details Code B2-03 Level B2 · Module B2.1 News and institutions of the European Communities Prerequisites B2-01, B2-02; INT-02 (institutions); B1-08 and B1-16 (basic political lexicon); B1-13 (numbers) Estimated time 20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 164–167), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, root dictionary, chronometer, voice synthesis script, tutor sessions Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. understand and report a complete electoral news: turnout, results, seats, ballots, disputes; 2. follow the stages of a government crisis and the formation of a government (office, consultations, confidence, batter); 3. distinguishing the names of the offices and procedures in the different Arab countries and translating them with Italian equivalents corrected; 4. recognizing the lexicon of political positions (majority, opposition, coalition, currents) without add judgments; 5. read a political service of 350 words at least 80 words per minute and summarize it in a neutral manner. Four-week plan. title: Economic and commercial lexicon
text: Lesson overview The economic pages of Arabic newspapers have a fixed vocabulary and many numbers: growth, inflation, interest rates, budget, debt, exchange rate, foreign trade, business, stock exchange. In this unit learn to read and report an economic news with precision: indicators, the verbs of movement (to climb up, to descend, to stabilize), expressions of comparison over time (to be based annually on the same period as last year) the vocabulary of enterprises and trade, and the difference between a given and an interpretation. Countries, companies and figures of texts are invented. Four weeks, in parallel with EGY-12. Item Details Code B2-04 Level B2 · Module B2.1 News and institutions of the European Communities Prerequisites B2-01 → B2-03; B1-10 (changes and comparisons), B1-13 (number), B1-16 (basic economic lexicon) Estimated time 20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 168–171), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, dictionary by root, chronometer, calculator, script for speech synthesis, tutor sessions Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. understanding and reporting the main economic indicators (GDP, growth, inflation, unemployment, debt, deficit, exchange rate, reserves); 2. describe variations and comparisons over time with the correct vocabulary and syntax (B1-10); 3. to read a report on monetary or budgetary policy and distinguish data, decisions and interpretations; 4. understanding the vocabulary of companies, foreign trade and markets; 5. read an economic service of 350 words at least 80 words per minute and summarize it with figures Right. Four-week plan. Data, decision, interpretation Like you said. Šarīf, in economic news three levels coexist: the data ( ⁧أَعْلَنَ الجِهَازُ⁩ … ⁧أَنَّ التَّضَخُّمَ بَلَغَ⁩ ...), the decision ( ⁧قَرَّرَ البَنْكُ المَرْكَزِيُّ⁩ ...), interpretation ( ⁧يَرَى مُحَلِّلُونَ أَنَّ⁩ … · ⁧يُعْزَى ذٰلِكَ إِلَى⁩ …). title: Legal and administrative lexicon
text: Lesson overview The judicial chronicle and the administrative texts have a very precise Arabic: each word has a technical value, and an approximate translation ('condemned' by 'defendant', 'final judgment' by 'first-degree judgment') changes the meaning of the news. In this unit you learn the vocabulary of courts and of the stages of a trial as the press tells you, the language of regulatory texts (articles of law, "is forbidden" , "is allowed," "except"), the vocabulary of administrative documents and practices and the rules of prudence to report a judicial case (presumption of innocence, attribution). The cases of the texts are invented and concern only civil and administrative matters or public events told by the newspapers. Four weeks, in parallel with EGY-13. Item Details Code B2-05 Level B2 · Module B2.1 News and institutions of the European Communities Prerequisites B2-01 → B2-04; INT-02 (powers, official acts); B1-05 (passive); A2-08 (documents) Estimated time 20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 172–175), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, root dictionary, voice synthesis scripts, tutor sessions Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. understand a judicial news: courts, parties, stages of the trial, types of judgment, appeals; 2. a precise distinction between accused and convicted, first and final judgment, prosecution and evidence, and to report them in compliance with the presumption of innocence; 3. read an article in law or regulation: numbering, obligations, prohibitions, exceptions, entry into force; 4. understanding the vocabulary of documents and administrative practices (release, renewal, legalization, appeal); 5. read a judicial or administrative service of 350 words at least 80 words per minute. Four-week plan. title: Security and defence lexicon (in the media)
text: Lesson overview Security and defence occupy part of the Arab news daily: ministries and armed forces, cooperation agreements, border crises, ceasefires, attacks and investigations. To understand these news and report them accurately, a specific vocabulary is needed, but above all caution is needed: the budgets of victims change from hour to hour, sources are often not verifiable, and the choice of a word (the "fighter," the "militian" or "terrorist") often reveals the point of view of those who write. In this unit you learn the vocabulary of the security institutions and the news about them, the prepositions of cause and circumstance typical of the chronicle, the way to report uncertain budgets and figures and the rules to bring back the words connotationed without making them own. The vocabulary is that of the newspapers: no technical or operational details. Three weeks, no trace of variety in parallel. Item Details Code B2-06 Level B2 · Module B2.1 News and institutions of the European Communities Prerequisites B2-01 → B2-05; B1 (information and security lexicon); INT-01 (assignment and prudence) Estimated time 16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 176–178) Materials This unit, root dictionary, voice synthesis scripts, tutor sessions Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognising security and defence institutions and their names in different countries; 2. understand news about cooperation, crisis, ceasefire and investigation, with prepositions of cause and condition ( ⁧إِثْرَ⁩ , ⁧جَرَّاءَ⁩ , ⁧عَلَى خَلْفِيَّةِ⁩ …); 3. reporting uncertain budgets and figures with the right formulas ( ⁧حَصِيلَة⁩ , ⁧مَا لَا يَقِلُّ عَنْ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَتَسَنَّ التَّحَقُّقُ⁩ …); 4. recognize the words and bring them back to the source; 5. read a news report of 330 words on these topics at least 80 words per minute. Three-week plan. title: Diplomacy: summits, communiqués and joint statements
text: Lesson overview Diplomacy uses a coded language. A ‘frank’ meeting is one in which the parties disagree; ‘agreeing to continue consultations’ often means that no agreement has been reached; and ‘expresses concern’, ‘condemns’ and ‘strongly condemns’ sit at distinct points on a scale. Anyone reading open sources needs to understand this code without exaggerating or overlooking its nuances. In this unit, you will learn the vocabulary of visits and summits, the ‘thermometer’ of diplomatic adjectives, the scale of verbs used in communiqués and resolutions, the structure of a joint statement (including clauses introduced by ⁧إِذْ⁩ ), diplomatic actions (summoning an ambassador, recalling one, severing relations) and how to read what a communiqué leaves unsaid. The sources in the texts are fictional; the writing exercise uses a real public communiqué. Two weeks. Item Details Code INT-03 Level B2 · Track INT · Module B2.1 Prerequisites INT-01 (assignment, prudence); INT-02 (institutions, securities); B2-03 (political lexicon); B2-06 Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 179–180) Materials This unit, official sites in Arabic (for the exercise 11), session with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. understand news about visits, talks and summits and their fixed formulas; 2. interpret the adjectives of the diplomatic thermometer and make them in English without exaggerating or mitigating; 3. recognize the scale of verbs in a statement or resolution (from ⁧يُرَحِّبُ⁩ a ⁧يُدِينُ بِشِدَّةٍ⁩ ); 4. read the structure of a joint declaration: preamble by ⁧إِذْ⁩ and device; 5. note what a statement fails to say and report it with caution. title: Understanding an Interview
text: Lesson overview Interviews are one of the richest and most insidious sources: the interviewed person speaks firsthand, but chooses what to say and what to keep quiet, and the journalist chooses what to ask and what to publish. In this unit you learn the genres of the interview (printed, television, radio), the types of question and their purpose, the characteristics of fuṣḥā spoken (falling desires, filling words, self-corrections), the techniques by which an interviewee avoids a question and the way to report precisely what has been said and what has not been said. Four weeks, in parallel with the end of EGY-13 and the beginning of EGY-14. Item Details Code B2-07 Level B2 · Module B2.2 Attribution and certainty Prerequisites Module B2.1; INT-01 (assignment); B1-23 (Conversation strategies) Estimated time 20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 182–185), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, script for vocal synthesis, extracts of radio or television interviews in fuṣḥā (Appendix C), sessions with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize the genres of the interview and their conventions (demand and answer, introduction, title); 2. classify questions (open, closed, in-depth, oriented) and understand what they are looking for; 3. follow the fuṣḥā talk of an interview, with its simplifications and its filling words; 4. recognize when an interviewee does not respond, and how he does so; 5. report an interview with the right verbs, including waste and non-answers ( ⁧رَفَضَ التَّعْلِيقَ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَسْتَبْعِدْ⁩ ). Four-week plan. title: Recorded speech and attribution verbs
text: Lesson overview Much of a newspaper article is made up of other people's words: statements, communications, sources. The journalist cannot bring them back without choosing a verb, and the verb is never neutral: "he said" , "he affirmed" , "he admitted" , "he sustained" , "he claimed" give to the same sentence a different weight. In this unit you systematically study the discourse reported in Arabic (statements, questions, orders), the scale of the verbs of attribution from the most neutral to the most burden of judgment, the types of source (declared, anonymous, concordant, social) and the way to make all this in English without losing or adding anything. It is the basic grammar of work on open sources. Four weeks, in parallel with EGY-14. Item Details Code B2-08 Level B2 · Module B2.2 Attribution and certainty Prerequisites B2-07; INT-01 (assignment and prudence); B1-09 (ḥāl) Estimated time 20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 186–189), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)67), voice synthesis scripts, tutor sessions Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. transforming direct discourse into indirect and vice versa: statements ( ⁧إِنَّ⁩ / ⁧أَنَّ⁩ ), applications ( ⁧عَمَّا إِذَا⁩ ), orders ( ⁧طَلَبَ⁩ … ⁧أَنْ⁩ ); 2. classify the attribution verbs according to the force and position of the journalist ( ⁧قَالَ⁩ · ⁧أَكَّدَ⁩ · ⁧اِعْتَرَفَ⁩ · ⁧زَعَمَ⁩ · ⁧نَفَى⁩ …); 3. recognising and evaluating source types ( ⁧مَصْدَرٌ مُطَّلِعٌ⁩ , ⁧مَصَادِرُ مُتَطَابِقَةٌ⁩ , ⁧نَقْلًا عَنْ⁩ …); 4. translating the speech in English with the timing and, where necessary, the conditional journalistic; 5. compare two reports of the same statement and show where they differ. title: Mode and degree of certainty
text: Lesson overview Between the Minister will resign, the Minister may resign, it is likely that the Minister will resign and ... it is not excluded that the Minister resigns... there is all the difference between a news and a hypothesis. The Arabic print has a rich and precise system to scale the certainty: particles ( ⁧قَدْ⁩ , ⁧رُبَّمَا⁩ , ⁧لَعَلَّ⁩ ), expressions with ⁧مِنَ⁩ ( ⁧مِنَ المُرَجَّحِ⁩ , ⁧مِنَ المُحْتَمَلِ⁩ , ⁧مِنَ المُؤَكَّدِ⁩ ), impersonal verbs ( ⁧يُرَجَّحُ⁩ , ⁧يُعْتَقَدُ⁩ , ⁧يَبْدُو⁩ ), compulsory and waiting formulas ( ⁧يَجِبُ⁩ , ⁧يَنْبَغِي⁩ , ⁧مِنَ المُفْتَرَضِ⁩ ). In this unit you build a scale of certainty in Arabic and English, learn to distinguish the possibility from obligation and prediction, and practice not to raise or lower the degree of certainty when you translate or summarize. Three weeks, in parallel with EGY-14 and EGY-15. Item Details Code B2-09 Level B2 · Module B2.2 Attribution and certainty Prerequisites B2-07, B2-08; B1-11 (hypothetical period) Estimated time 16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 190–192), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)68), voice synthesis scripts, tutor sessions Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. distinguish ⁧قَدْ⁩ + imperfect (possibility) from ⁧قَدْ⁩ + perfect (compense, emphasis); 2. place on a five-step scale the most frequent expressions of certainty in printing; 3. to distinguish the mode of knowledge (probably) from that of duty (need) and waiting (should, is expected); 4. translate each step with the right Italian equivalent, without raising it or lowering it; 5. write a short perspective analysis with explicit and attributed degrees of certainty. title: Argumentative texts
text: Lesson overview The articles of opinion ( ⁧مَقَالُ رَأْيٍ⁩ ), editorials ( ⁧اِفْتِتَاحِيَّة⁩ ) and headings ( ⁧عَمُود⁩ ) are the part of the newspaper in which it is discussed: the author supports a thesis, brings arguments, responds to objections and draws a conclusion. For an analyst they are valuable, because they show how to think in a country about a topic; But they must be read knowing how to distinguish the thesis from the arguments, the solid arguments from the weak ones, the apparent concession from the true. In this unit you learn the structure of an argumentative text , the correlations of the cause , consequence , addition and concession ( ⁧فَضْلًا عَنْ⁩ , ⁧وَمِنْ ثَمَّ⁩ , ⁧صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ⁩ … ⁧إِلَّا أَنَّ⁩ …, ⁧وَإِذَا كَانَ⁩ … ⁧فَإِنَّ⁩ ...), the most frequent types of argument and fallacies, and start writing your own argumentative text. Four weeks, in parallel with EGY-15. Item Details Code B2-10 Level B2 · Module B2.2 Attribution and certainty Prerequisites B2-07 → B2-09; B1-20 (connective); B1-21 (Summary) Estimated time 20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 193–196), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)69), voice synthesis scripts, tutor sessions Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. identify in an article of opinion thesis, arguments, examples, objections, rebuttals and conclusion; 2. use and recognize the argumentative connections of fuṣḥā, including concessionary constructions ( ⁧صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ⁩ … ⁧إِلَّا أَنَّ⁩ … · ⁧وَإِذَا كَانَ⁩ … ⁧فَإِنَّ⁩ …); 3. classify the arguments (data, e.g. authorities, consequences, comparison) and assess their soundness; 4. recognizing the most common fallacies (generalization, false dilemma, attack on the person); 5. write an argumentative text of 250 words with a clear structure. Four-week plan. title: Implicate connotation and expressions
text: Lesson overview A text can judge without ever saying "in my opinion." Simply choose the "Removement" instead of "Protesta" , "Crollo" instead of "calo" , "Removement" instead of "government" , one final "-', one "---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- One metaphor is enough (the ball is in the field of government ,      , throw gasoline on the fire ,). In this unit you learn to recognize the connotation of Arabic press words, the most frequent idiomatic metaphors and expressions, the signals of implicit (presumptions, ironic quotes, rhetorical questions, irony) and the way to translate them without mitigating or exaggerating them. Three weeks, in parallel with EGY-15 and the beginning of ARZ-01. Item Details Code B2-11 Level B2 · Module B2.2 Attribution and certainty Prerequisites B2-08 → B2-10; B2-03 (Evaluative lexicon); B2-06 (speaks spoken) Estimated time 16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 197–199), plus the EGY and ARZ track in separate blocks Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)70), voice synthesis scripts, tutor sessions Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. place the words of printing on a neutral/positive/negative scale and choose the Italian equivalent the same level; 2. recognizing and translating about twenty metaphors and idiomatic expressions in printing; 3. Identifying assumptions ( ⁧أَخِيرًا⁩ , ⁧مَرَّةً أُخْرَى⁩ , ⁧مَا زَالَ⁩ , ⁧حَتَّى⁩ ) and what they suggest; 4. recognizing ironic quotes, rhetorical questions and irony; 5. to say, in a note of analysis, what a text suggests without saying it, distinguishing it from what he says. title: Facts and opinions: language markers
text: Lesson overview This unit closes the work of the module B2.2 and transforms it into a method. In each text there are facts (verifiables), statements (attributed to someone), interpretations (linking facts) and opinions (value judgments). The language signals them with precise markers, but sometimes it confuses them on purpose: "It is evident that """ """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" In this unit you learn to recognize the markers of each category, to expose opinions disguised as facts, to distinguish established cause and hypothetical cause, and to build a note of analysis in English that separates the four levels. Three weeks, in parallel with ARZ-01 and the beginning of EGY-16. Item Details Code B2-12 Level B2 · Module B2.2 Attribution and certainty Prerequisites B2-07 → B2-11; INT-01 (assignment, prudence); B2-04 (date, decision, interpretation) Estimated time 16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 200–202), plus the ARZ/EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)71), four color markers, voice synthesis scripts, tutor sessions Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. categorize the sentences of a text in facts, statements, interpretations and opinions, with the markers which the report; 2. recognising the views presented as facts ( ⁧مِنَ الوَاضِحِ أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧الحَقِيقَةُ أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧مِمَّا يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ⁩ ); 3. distinguish a causal relationship established by a proven one; 4. identify what a text does not say (lacune) and what it would take to verify it; 5. write a note of analysis in English with the four separate levels. The four levels Level What is it? How it happens Example done ( ⁧وَاقِعَة⁩ · ⁧مَعْلُومَة⁩ ) what has happened or exists, verifiable documents, data, more independent sources ⁧أَعْلَنَ البَنْكُ المَرْكَزِيُّ رَفْعَ⁩ ⁧سِعْرِ الفَائِدَةِ.⁩ declaration ( ⁧تَصْرِيح⁩ ) what someone said that he said it was a fact; What it says has to be verified ⁧قَالَ الوَزِيرُ إِنَّ الأَسْعَارَ⁩ ⁧سَتَسْتَقِرُّ.⁩ interpretation ( ⁧تَفْسِير⁩ · ⁧تَحْلِيل⁩ ) a link between facts: cause, effect, meaning with data, comparisons, method ⁧يُرْجِعُ خُبَرَاءُ ذٰلِكَ إِلَى⁩ ⁧ارْتِفَاعِ الطَّلَبِ.⁩ opinion ( ⁧رَأْي⁩ · ⁧حُكْم⁩ ) a value judgement or proposal does not occur: is shared or not ⁧وَهُوَ قَرَارٌ جَرِيءٌ يَسْتَحِقُّ⁩ ⁧الإِشَادَةَ.⁩ One sentence, more levels. title: Conflicts and humanitarian crisis in the news
text: Lesson overview News about humanitarian crises is among the most read and hard to report: figures are estimates, sources are often involved, words have a legal weight (refugeed, displaced, famine, war crime) and a translation error can change the sense of a relationship. In this unit you learn the humanitarian vocabulary of the press and UN agencies (displacement, access, food security, appeals and funding), the Arab names of the main organizations, the precise distinction between refugee, internally displaced, asylum seeker and migrant, and the way to treat terms with legal or technical value, which are always attributed to those who are competent to use them. The vocabulary is that of public news and communications: no operational details. Two weeks. Item Details Code INT-04 Level B2 · Track INT · Module B2.2 Prerequisites B2-06 (security and defence in the media); B2-08 → B2-12; INT-01 → INT-03 Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 203–204), plus the ARZ/EGY track Materials This unit, the news page in Arabic of the United Nations and the sites in Arabic of humanitarian agencies (Appendix C), session with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. understanding news and communications about humanitarian crises: needs, access, aid, appeals, funding; 2. recognizing the Arab names of the main humanitarian organisations and their Italian acronyms; 3. to distinguish precisely refugees, displaced persons, asylum seekers, migrants and stateless persons; 4. To treat terms with technical or legal value with caution ( ⁧مَجَاعَة⁩ , ⁧جَرَائِمُ حَرْبٍ⁩ ...), assigning them; 5. report humanitarian figures with the source, type of data (estimate, registration, projection) and date. Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · ...Insecurity of food ... ........... Luca is on video call with Laylā, which is preparing a report on the humanitarian situation in the northern provinces of an imaginary country (B2-06). In my work I write exactly what the agencies say, and I quote the name of the agency and the date of the report. ⁧هَلْ هٰذَا⁩ :« ⁧مِلْيُونَا شَخْصٍ يَحْتَاجُونَ إِلَى مُسَاعَدَاتٍ⁩ » ⁧وَالأَرْقَامُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧رَقْمٌ دَقِيقٌ؟⁩ What about the numbers? Is that precise? ⁧يُقَدَّرُ عَدَدُ المُحْتَاجِينَ⁩ » ⁧هُوَ تَقْدِيرٌ، لَا إِحْصَاءٌ. الوَكَالَاتُ تَقُولُ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ .« ⁧يُقَدَّرُ⁩ » ⁧وَيَجِبُ أَنْ نَنْقُلَ كَلِمَةَ⁩ .«… ⁧بِـ⁩ Laylā: It's an estimate, not a census. The agencies say that the number of people in need is estimated to be... And we have to quote the word "value" itself. ⁧كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ لَهَا وَزْنُهَا.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luke: Every word has its weight. ⁧فِي هٰذِهِ الأَخْبَارِ، وَرَاءَ كُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ أُنَاسٌ حَقِيقِيُّونَ. لِذٰلِكَ الدِّقَّةُ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧وَاجِبٌ.⁩ Laylā: In this news, there are real people behind every word. Dialogue 2 · Refugees, displaced persons, asylum seekers At the police station, Nādya, the interpreter, corrects with Luke the glossary that they are preparing for the door. The vocabulary serves to understand and translate public news and documents. The status of a real person is determined by the competent authorities in accordance with legal procedures: the translator makes the word used in the source exactly, without replacing it. 7. title: Disinformation: language signals and verification
text: Lesson overview In the Arab information ecosystem, false, misleading or deleted content circulates daily alongside news: messages sent in family groups, old photos presented as new, invented quotes, sites that mimic real newspapers. There is also an Arab journalistic genre dedicated to verification ( ⁧تَدْقِيقُ المَعْلُومَاتِ⁩ ), with a vocabulary and its own structure. In this unit learn the types of misinformation and their Arabic names, language signals that make a content suspicious, verification steps as they are described by fact-checking platforms, and the vocabulary of the verification articles ( ⁧الاِدِّعَاء⁩ , ⁧التَّقْيِيم⁩ , ⁧مُضَلِّل⁩ , ⁧خَارِجَ سِيَاقِهِ⁩ ). The method is the public one of media education: no operational technique. Two weeks. Item Details Code INT-05 Level B2 · Track INT · Module B2.2 Prerequisites B2-08 → B2-12; INT-04; EGY-12 (news and voices) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 205–206), plus the ARZ/EGY track Materials This unit, Arab news verification platforms (Appendix C), session with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. appoint and distinguish the main types of misinformation in Arabic; 2. recognizing the linguistic signals of a suspicious content (urgency, emotion, vague sources, appeals to sharing); 3. describe in Arabic the steps of a verification: source, date, author, context, comparison; 4. read an Arabic fact-checking article and report the verdict precisely; 5. write a brief verification of an invented content, with the vocabulary and structure of the genre. Two-week plan. A signal is not evidence. A text full of exclamation points can be true, and a sober text can be false. The signals tell you how much to verify, not what is true. 4. The steps of verification Over Arabic Question 1 · the source ⁧مَنْ نَشَرَ المُحْتَوَى أَوَّلًا؟⁩ Who published it first? It's recognizable, does it have a story? 2 · the date ⁧مَتَى نُشِرَ؟⁩ Is it recent? is connected to an actual event? 3 · the author ⁧مَنْ كَتَبَهُ أَوْ قَالَهُ؟⁩ Is it real? Is he competent? Did he really say that? Over Arabic Question 4 · the context ⁧مَا السِّيَاقُ الأَصْلِيُّ؟⁩ where and when was the content (photo, video, sentence) born? 5 · comparison ⁧هَلْ نَشَرَتْهُ مَصَادِرُ مَوْثُوقَةٌ أُخْرَى؟⁩ Do they report reliable and independent sources? 6 · the primary source ⁧هَلْ هُنَاكَ بَيَانٌ رَسْمِيٌّ أَوْ وَثِيقَةٌ؟⁩ Is it on the institution's website, in the original document? title: Translation from Arabic: method
text: Lesson overview With the module B2.3 translation becomes the center of work. So far you have translated sentences to verify understanding; now learn to produce a professional translation: faithful in content, natural in English, verifiable. An Arabic journalistic text translated word by word gives a heavy and sometimes wrong Italian: very long sentences linked by In this unit you learn a method in four phases (understand, disassemble, reformulate, revise) and the most frequent transformations between Arabic and Italian: from maṣdar to the verb, from the chain of ⁧و⁩ to Italian periods, from ḥāl to the gerund, from the passive with ⁧تَمَّ⁩ Italian forms, repetitions to synonyms and pronouns. A new teacher leads you, the professor. Ṭāhā ʿAbd al-ḤamīdEgyptian translator. Four weeks, in parallel with the start of EGY-17. Item Details Code B2-13 Level B2 · Module B2.3 Translated by: Prerequisites Modules B2.1 and B2.2; B2-02 (long-term syntax) Estimated time 20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 208–211), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)72), dictionary by root, a monolingual Italian dictionary, sessions with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. to apply to a text of 200 words a four-step translation method; 2. divide a long Arabic period into natural Italian periods, preserving logical relationships; 3. apply frequent transformations (maṣdar → verb, ḥāl → gerund or relative, ⁧تَمَّ⁩ + maṣdar → passive, repetition → pronoun or synonym); 4. treat own names, titles, dates, numbers and quotations according to Italian conventions; 5. review a translation with a checklist and evaluate it with the Accuracy / Return section. Four-week plan. The four phases Phase Arabic What are you doing? 1 · Understand ⁧الفَهْم⁩ read the entire text twice; gender, sources, thesis; look for words you don't know (dictionary by root) 2 · dismount ⁧التَّحْلِيل⁩ for each period: main verbs, subjects, logical relationships (cause, purpose, concession); signs i maṣdar, i ḥāl, i ⁧تَمَّ⁩ 3 · reword ⁧إِعَادَةُ⁩ ⁧الصِّيَاغَةِ⁩ write in English starting from the way, period by period, choosing Italian order and forms 4 · review ⁧المُرَاجَعَة⁩ comparisons with the original (nothing added, nothing lost), then read only Italian aloud The phase 4 It's done twice. title: Translation from Arabic: journalistic texts
text: Lesson overview In B2-13 You've learned the method. Now apply it to the genres of the newspaper, each with his own problems: the title (short, nominal, sometimes with word games), the attack of the news, the quotations, the interview, the editorial with his metaphors, the official speech with formulas of courtesy and religious formulas. You also learn a fundamental distinction for those who work with open sources: integral translation (all, faithfully) and synthesis translation (gisting: the essential, in little space, without betraying). And learn when and how to add a translator's note. Four weeks, in parallel with EGY-17. Item Details Code B2-14 Level B2 · Module B2.3 Translated by: Prerequisites B2-13; B1-15 (the language of the licences); B2-07, B2-10, B2-11; INT-02INT-03 Estimated time 20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 212–215), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)55, G72), dictionary by root, sessions with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. translate an Arabic title with the conventions of Italian titles; 2. Translate attacks, quotes and interviews while retaining attributions and register; 3. translating an editorial by preserving tone, metaphors and argumentation; 4. translate the formulas of courtesy and religious of official speeches in an exact and neutral manner; 5. choose between complete translation and synthesis translation, and write a faithful summary of 100 words from a Article 400. Four-week plan. Titles Arabic title Structure English rendering ⁧الحُكُومَةُ تَرْفَعُ الدَّعْمَ عَنِ الوَقُودِ⁩ name + verb at present Government takes out fuel subsidies ⁧رَفْعُ الدَّعْمِ عَنِ الوَقُودِ ابْتِدَاءً مِنْ يَنَايِرَ⁩ maṣdar (G55) Fuel subsidies from January ⁧وَزِيرُ الخَارِجِيَّةِ فِي رُومَا⁩ nominal sentence without verb The Minister of Foreign Affairs in Rome ⁧الرَّئِيسُ يَتَحَدَّى⁩ …« ⁧لَنْ نَتَرَاجَعَ⁩ » ⁧المُعَارَضَةَ⁩ quote + title "We won't go back": the president challenges the opposition ⁧هَلْ تَنْجَحُ الوَسَاطَةُ؟⁩ application Will mediation succeed? ⁧الجِسْرُ يَرَى النُّورَ⁩ … ⁧بَعْدَ عَشْرِ سَنَوَاتٍ⁩ dots, metaphor After ten years the bridge sees the light ⁧مَصْرَعُ ثَلَاثَةٍ فِي حَادِثِ سَيْرٍ⁩ maṣdar Three deaths in a car accident ⁧يَتَحَدَّى⁩ • Challenge ⁧مَصْرَع⁩ • death (violent) • death (in the headlines). The rules. 1) Translate the title last, after you understand the article. 2) Use the forms of Italian titles: present, nominal sentences, two points. 3) It retains the degree of certainty and quotes (a title with a quote is a quote, not a statement in the newspaper). 4) Keep the metaphor if the Italian has an equivalent; Otherwise make sense. 5) Do not add any emphasis ('choc', 'bufera'), which the original does not have. 3. If in Arabic it is quoted only ⁧لَنْ تَتَرَاجَعَ⁩ In English, quotes only go          'it will not backtrack: widening or restricting the quotation changes what the source said. 4. Interviews and editorials The interview (B2-07). The applications are translated into the "Lei" (Arab courtesy plural); the responses of fuṣḥā Talked, they are cleaned out of useless fillers, but significant hesitations are preserved ( ⁧بِصَرَاحَةٍ⁩ , ⁧يَعْنِي⁩ ... before a delicate response) and self-corrections that change a given. In the printed translation, applications shall remain bold or preceded by the name of the newspaper. The editorial (B2-10, B2-11). It is the most difficult kind, because it counts the tone: irony, metaphors, rhetorical questions, proverbs. The rules: preserves the argumentative structure (thesis, concessions, conclusion); make metaphors with Italian equivalents; keep the ironic quotes; do not attenuate or exaggerate judgments. An Arabic editorial may seem emphatic to an Italian reader: the translation does not correct it, it makes it. The emphatic vocabulary. Many adjectives and adverbs of Arab prose are more frequent than in English: ⁧بَالِغ⁩ ( ⁧بَالِغُ الأَهَمِّيَّةِ⁩ • of extreme importance () ⁧شَدِيد⁩ , ⁧كَبِير⁩ , ⁧عَمِيق⁩ . If Arabic is the usual formula, a corresponding intensity can be used in English without doubling it. 5. Pronunciation The title aloud. Titles ( ⁧فَخَامَة⁩ , ⁧مَعَالِي⁩ , speech, Italian equivalent letter in the full text; omitted in the article (INT-02) ⁧سَعَادَة⁩ ) The translator's note (N.d.T.). It is added, in square brackets or at the foot of the page, only when the Italian reader needs information to understand the text: a game of intransducible words, a cultural reference (the Country of the Nile) a term that has two possible translations, a quote. Full translation and synthesis translation  Integral Synthesis (gisting) purpose make the whole text give the essential in little space length like the original 20–30% of the original what is left all main facts, sources, positions, key figures, general tone what you lose none details, repetitions, secondary examples what you never do — add, interpret, change the degree of certainty or attribution shape continuous text short text or points, with reference to the source When you use synthesis. When examining many texts and deciding which to translate in full; in a press review; when the reader has to know what an article is talking about. Synthesis is not a free summary: it is a reduced translation, and the same ethics as integral translation is valid. Quotes, if reported, remain textual. A scheme for synthesis. title: Translation to Arabic: simple texts
text: Lesson overview Translating to Arabic is more difficult than translating from Arabic: the Italian "tire" the Arabic phrase towards its structures, and the result is an Arabic understandable but full of casts: the article in the wrong place, the Italian preposition translated to the letter, the order of the Italian words, the wrong agreements with the plural of things. At level B2 The goal is realistic: to translate simple and short texts (warnings, formal messages, short news) into a correct and clear Arabic, using as a model the Arabic texts you know. In this unit learn the basic rules of translation to Arabic (G73), the prepositions that change from one language to another, the most frequent casts and the method of parallel texts. Four weeks, in parallel with the end of EGY-17 and the beginning of EGY-18. Item Details Code B2-15 Level B2 · Module B2.3 Translated by: Prerequisites B2-13, B2-14; B1-22 (the formal letter); B1-08 (order and agreement) Estimated time 20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 216–219), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)73), an Italian-Arabic dictionary, Arabic texts from previous units such as models, sessions with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. build correctly in Arabic iḍāfa, agreements (including with pluralities of things), numbers and relative; 2. Choose the order of Arabic words and connections suitable for a journalistic or administrative text; 3. use the right Arab prepositions with the most frequent verbs, without limestone the Italian; 4. recognizing and correcting the most common casts from English; 5. to translate a formal notice, message and short news of 80–120 words, using text parallel. Four-week plan. title: Texts which are not ambiguous
text: Lesson overview In B1-17 you have learned the five most frequent types of ambiguity of voiceless texts (active or passive, verb or name, simple or derived form, verb person, prefix or root) and a five-step strategy. Now that you're reading and translating long articles, you meet the most difficult cases: ⁧الكتاب⁩ which may be the book of the book or the writers of the book; an impersonal passive as ⁧يعلن عن⁩ ; an adjective that, after aiḍāfa, may refer to two names; a pronoun with two possible precedents; a proper name which is also a common word; the Egyptian prints, where they are written ⁧على⁩ It may also be the name ʿAlī. In this unit learn to use clues ( ⁧القرائن⁩ ) in a systematic way, to distinguish the ambiguity that arises from the lack of vowels from what remains also with vowels, and to manage in translation the unresolved cases and the ambiguity desired (G74). Three weeks, in parallel with EGY-18. Item Details Code B2-16 Level B2 · Module B2.3 Translated by: Prerequisites B1-17 (read without voice), B1-05 (the liabilities); B2-01 (reading method), B2-13 → B2-15 Estimated time 16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 220–222), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)74), a pencil to mark ambiguous words, sessions with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize, in addition to the five types of B1-17, the ambiguities of number, particle, own name and reference; 2. use seven clues (position, object complement, chord, placements, sense, frequency, text) for Choose the right reading; 3. recognising the impersonal liabilities and passive formulas of printing; 4. take into account graphic habits (hamza, alif maqṣūra, partial vowels) of the press; 5. vocalize only the necessary words in a text that you write or translate, and report in translation an unresolved ambiguity. Three-week plan. title: Spoken MSA and code switching
text: Lesson overview In talks, interviews and press conferences the fuṣḥā It doesn't sound like in the news: those who talk improvisingly drop almost all the endings, use the expressions of connection of the speech and pronounce some consonants in the way of their country. And often, in the same speech, passes from fuṣḥā to the dialect and returns: the data in fuṣḥā, the example in dialect, the line in dialect, the conclusion again in fuṣḥā. This passage is called code switching ( ⁧التَّنَاوُبُ اللُّغَوِيُّ⁩ ) and is not a mistake or lack of culture: it is an instrument with precise functions. In this unit learn how the fuṣḥā spoken (G)75), to recognize the signals of the passage to the dialect, to understand its function (G76) and to make it into translation. It is also the first unit of the module B2.4, dedicated to oral variation and production. Three weeks, while EGY concludes-18. Item Details Code B2-17 Level B2 · Module B2.4 Variation and production Prerequisites Modules B2.1 → B2.3; EGY-17 (Egyptian media) and EGY-18 in parallel Estimated time 16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 224–226), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)75, G76), talk shows and authentic interviews chosen by the tutor, a recorder, sessions with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. describe the differences between fuṣḥā read and fuṣḥā spoken (disclaimers, tanwīn, numbers, pronunciation, expressions of connection); 2. speak yourself in a fuṣḥā natural spoken, without unnecessary endings but with proper internal vowels; 3. recognizing in a speech the passage between fuṣḥā and dialect through ten signals; 4. explain the function of each step (given, example, bar, emotion, quote, conclusion); 5. translating a speech with code switching, making the log change and annotating it when It's okay, it's okay. Three-week plan. Dialogue 1 · One and a half languages Night class. Salmā lets the class listen to a piece (invented) of an Egyptian talk show. Arabic Translation ⁧اِسْمَعُوا هٰذَا المَقْطَعَ مِنْ بَرْنَامَجٍ حِوَارِيٍّ. الضَّيْفُ خَبِيرٌ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧اقْتِصَادِيٌّ مِصْرِيٌّ. لُوكَا، بِأَيِّ لُغَةٍ يَتَكَلَّمُ؟⁩ Salmā: Listen to this piece of a talk show. The guest is an Egyptian economist. Luca, what language do you speak? ⁧اِرْتَفَعَ مُعَدَّلُ التَّضَخُّمِ إِلَى خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ فِي⁩ » ⁧يَبْدَأُ بِالفُصْحَى:⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧هٰذَا⁩ .« ⁧يعني الناس مش قادرة تشتري اللحمة⁩ » ⁧ثُمَّ يَقُولُ:⁩ .« ⁧المِئَةِ⁩ ⁧مِصْرِيٌّ!⁩ Luke: Start in fuṣḥāThe inflation rate has risen to 15%». Then he says, "I'm gonna go."yaʿni in-nās miš ʾadra tištiri l-laḥma" (In short, people can't buy meat"). This is Egyptian! ⁧الاِنْتِقَالَ مِنْ مُسْتَوًى⁩ :« ⁧التَّنَاوُبَ اللُّغَوِيَّ⁩ » ⁧صَحِيحٌ. هٰذَا مَا نُسَمِّيهِ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧لُغَوِيٍّ إِلَى آخَرَ فِي الكَلَامِ نَفْسِهِ. لِمَاذَا انْتَقَلَ فِي رَأْيِكَ؟⁩ Salmā: Right. This is what we call code "commutation": the transition from one language level to another in the same speech. Why do you think he went to the Egyptian? ⁧رُبَّمَا لِيُقَرِّبَ الفِكْرَةَ مِنَ النَّاسِ؟ الرَّقْمُ بِالفُصْحَى، وَالمِثَالُ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧بِالعَامِّيَّةِ.⁩ Luca: Maybe to bring the idea closer to people? The data in fuṣḥā, the example in dialect. ⁧أَحْسَنْتَ. الفُصْحَى لِلْأَرْقَامِ وَالتَّعْرِيفَاتِ وَالخُلَاصَاتِ، وَالعَامِّيَّةُ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧لِلْأَمْثِلَةِ وَالنُّكَتِ وَالمَشَاعِرِ. وَهَلْ لَاحَظْتَ شَيْئًا فِي فُصْحَاهُ؟⁩ Salmā: Bravo. title: Talk shows and debates: the passive Levantine
text: Lesson overview Lebanese talk shows are among the most followed in the Arab world, and the Levantine (Lebanese, Syrian, Palestinian, Jordanian) is, after the Egyptian, the dialect that feels most in the media. You don't have to learn to speak: you have to understand it enough to follow a debate, recognize positions and report them. The good news is that you already know the fuṣḥā and the Egyptian: the Levantine is close to both, and with a dozen grammatical words, some pronunciation rules and formulas typical of the debate you can understand much more than you think. In this unity learn the main traits of the Levant (sounds, pronouns, verbs, negation, interrogative words), the lexicon of the debate (breaking, granting, rejecting) and a method to follow a discussion in which everyone speaks together. Three weeks, while the Moroccan track begins (MAG-01). Item Details Code B2-18 Level B2 · Module B2.4 Variation and production Prerequisites B2-17 (fuṣḥā Talking and switching); B2-07 (interviews); the EGY track Estimated time 16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 227–229), plus the MAG track in separate blocks Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)77), talk show authentic levantini chosen by the tutor, a Levant speaker for scripts, sessions with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize the Levantine and distinguish it from the Egyptian and the fuṣḥā; 2. understand the main traits: pronunciation, pronouns and suffixes, present with b- and ʿam, future with raḥ, denial, interrogative words; 3. follow a Levant television debate, identifying who claims what and with what arguments and figures; 4. understand the formulas of the debate: interrupt, ask for the floor, grant, reject, thank; 5. report in fuṣḥā, neutrally, a debate heard in Levantine. Three-week plan. title: Vocabulary of media and communication
text: Lesson overview From B2-01 read articles, press releases and interviews: it is time to give a precise name to the world that produces them. A editorial staff has its roles (the editor, the editor, the correspondent, who checks the facts) and its genres (the inquiry, the editorial, the column, the scoop); traditional printing changes (downloads, digital subscriptions, layoffs, newsletters); social platforms have a new vocabulary, which Arabic has created in a few years ( ⁧تغريدة⁩ , ⁧وسم⁩ , ⁧مؤثر⁩ , ⁧خوارزمية⁩ ); institutional communication has its tools (the spokesperson, the campaigns, public relations). In this unit you learn this vocabulary by field , the most frequent placements ( ⁧اِنْتَشَرَ عَلَى نِطَاقٍ وَاسِعٍ⁩ , ⁧الأَكْثَرُ تَدَاوُلًا⁩ ) and the way in which Arabic forms neologisms (limestone, adaptation, new word from an ancient root). Three weeks, in parallel with MAG-01. Item Details Code B2-19 Level B2 · Module B2.4 Variation and production Prerequisites B2-01 (read an article), B2-07 and B2-08 (interviews, attribution), INT-05 (disinformation) Estimated time 16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 230–232), plus the MAG track in separate blocks Materials This unit, websites of Arab newspapers and televisions (Appendix C), sessions with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. appoint the roles of a editorial staff and major journalistic genres; 2. understand and use the vocabulary of the crisis and the transformation of the press (copies, subscriptions, dismissals, Newsletter); 3. understand and use the vocabulary of social platforms (post, tweet, follower, hashtag, algorithm, content Sponsored); 4. understand the vocabulary of institutional communication (spokesman, campaign, public relations, survey); 5. recognize how Arab neologisms of the media form. Three-week plan.
