Dialogue 1 · In the editorial staff Video call with Beirut. Laylā shows Luca the editorial staff of the information site he writes for. Arabic Translation ⁧هُنَا قَاعَةُ التَّحْرِيرِ. ذٰلِكَ رَئِيسُ التَّحْرِيرِ، هُوَ الَّذِي يُقَرِّرُ مَا⁩ : ⁧اُنْظُرْ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧يُنْشَرُ وَيَكْتُبُ الاِفْتِتَاحِيَّةَ.⁩ Laylā: Look: this is the editorial staff. That is the editor-in-chief: he decides what is published and writes the editorial. ⁧وَالشَّبَابُ أَمَامَ الشَّاشَاتِ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ What about the kids in front of the screens? ⁧مُحَرِّرُونَ. يَسْتَقْبِلُونَ الأَخْبَارَ مِنَ الوَكَالَاتِ وَمِنْ مُرَاسِلِينَا فِي⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧المَنَاطِقِ، وَيُعِيدُونَ صِيَاغَتَهَا. وَفِي الزَّاوِيَةِ قِسْمُ التَّحَقُّقِ: ثَلَاثَةُ زُمَلَاءَ⁩ ⁧يَتَحَقَّقُونَ مِنَ الصُّوَرِ وَالفِيدْيُوهَاتِ قَبْلَ النَّشْرِ.⁩ Laylā: Editors. They get news from agencies and correspondents in the regions, and they rewrite it. And in the corner there is the verification service: three colleagues check photos and videos before publication. ⁧وَأَنْتِ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ What about you? ⁧أَنَا أَكْتُبُ التَّحْقِيقَاتِ: مَوَاضِيعُ طَوِيلَةٌ تَحْتَاجُ إِلَى أَسَابِيعَ مِنَ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧البَحْثِ. وَأَكْتُبُ عَمُودًا أُسْبُوعِيًّا.⁩ Laylā: I write inquiries: long topics that require weeks of research. And I keep a weekly column. ⁧وَهَلْ حَقَّقْتِ سَبْقًا صَحَفِيًّا يَوْمًا؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luca: Have you ever had a scoop? ⁧مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً، قَبْلَ سَنَوَاتٍ. اليَوْمَ السَّبْقُ يَدُومُ دَقِيقَتَيْنِ:⁩ ( ⁧تَضْحَكُ⁩ ) ⁧لَيْلَى:⁩ ⁧تَنْشُرُهُ، وَبَعْدَ دَقِيقَتَيْنِ يَكُونُ فِي كُلِّ المَوَاقِعِ. لِذٰلِكَ نُفَضِّلُ أَنْ نَكُونَ⁩ ⁧الأَدَقَّ، لَا الأَسْرَعَ.⁩ Laylā: (laughs) Once, years ago. Today a scoop lasts two minutes: you publish it, and after two minutes it is on all sites. That's why we prefer to be the most precise, not the fastest. ⁧وَمَنْ يُمَوِّلُ المَوْقِعَ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luca: And who funds the site? ⁧الاِشْتِرَاكَاتُ وَالإِعْلَانَاتُ، وَمِنْحَةٌ مِنْ مُؤَسَّسَةٍ تَدْعَمُ الصَّحَافَةَ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ Laylā: Subscriptions and advertising, and a contribution from a foundation supporting the ⁧المُسْتَقِلَّةَ. هٰذَا يَحْمِي خَطَّنَا التَّحْرِيرِيَّ: لَا أَحَدَ يَقُولُ لَنَا مَاذَا نَكْتُبُ.⁩ Independent journalism. This protects our editorial line: no one tells us what to write. What to notice. ⁧قَاعَةُ التَّحْرِيرِ⁩ The editorial room is located at the end of the day. ⁧رَئِيسُ التَّحْرِيرِ⁩ The editor-in-chief, the director. ⁧الاِفْتِتَاحِيَّة⁩ The editorial (B2-14). ⁧مُحَرِّرُونَ⁩ • Editors • Editors ⁧مُرَاسِل⁩ . ⁧الزَّاوِيَة⁩ The angle is the same as the angle. ⁧قِسْمُ التَّحَقُّقِ⁩ The verification service (fact-checking) is used. ⁧التَّحْقِيقَات⁩ The investigation shall be carried out in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 21. ⁧عَمُود⁩ This item shall be entered in the register. ⁧سَبْقٌ صَحَفِيٌّ⁩ • Scoop: ⁧حَقَّقَ سَبْقًا⁩ It's a scoop. ⁧يَدُومُ⁩ It's hard. ⁧الأَدَقّ⁩ The most precise is the . ⁧يُمَوِّلُ⁩ The Commission shall adopt implementing acts in accordance with the procedure referred to in Article 21 (2). ⁧مِنْحَة⁩ (ii) aid, grant (iii) aid. ⁧الخَطُّ التَّحْرِيرِيُّ⁩ The editorial line is the same as the editorial line. 2. The editorial staff and the genres Role Arabic Genre Arabic director, editor-in-chief ⁧رَئِيسُ التَّحْرِيرِ⁩ news ⁧خَبَر⁩ editor ⁧مُحَرِّر⁩ service ⁧تَقْرِير⁩ corresponding ⁧مُرَاسِل⁩ investigation ⁧تَحْقِيقٌ صَحَفِيٌّ⁩ sent ⁧مَبْعُوث⁩ interview ⁧حِوَار⁩ · ⁧مُقَابَلَة⁩ independent journalist ⁧صَحَفِيٌّ مُسْتَقِلٌّ⁩ editorial ⁧اِفْتِتَاحِيَّة⁩ photojournalists ⁧مُصَوِّرٌ صَحَفِيٌّ⁩ address book ⁧عَمُود⁩ Verifier of the facts ⁧مُدَقِّقُ مَعْلُومَاتٍ⁩ Rule of opinion ⁧مَقَالُ رَأْيٍ⁩ holder ⁧مُذِيع⁩ · ⁧مُقَدِّم⁩ scoop ⁧سَبْقٌ صَحَفِيٌّ⁩ Locations. ⁧نَشَرَ خَبَرًا⁩ • to publish a news report • ⁧أَجْرَى مُقَابَلَةً⁩ / ⁧تَحْقِيقًا⁩ • do an interview / survey • ⁧حَقَّقَ سَبْقًا⁩ • make a scoop · ⁧كَشَفَ تَحْقِيقٌ أَنَّ⁩ ... an investigation revealed that... ⁧فِي اِفْتِتَاحِيَّتِهَا⁩ In his editorial, he wrote a newspaper. 3. The Changing Press English Arabic paper printing · digital edition ⁧النُّسْخَةُ الرَّقْمِيَّةُ⁩ · ⁧الصَّحَافَةُ الوَرَقِيَّةُ⁩ circulation, diffusion ⁧التَّوْزِيع⁩ · ⁧عَدَدُ النُّسَخِ⁩ decrease in sales ⁧تَرَاجُعُ المَبِيعَاتِ⁩ subscription · subscriber ⁧مُشْتَرِك⁩ · ⁧اِشْتِرَاك⁩ paywall ⁧حَائِطُ الدَّفْعِ⁩ · ⁧الاِشْتِرَاكُ المَدْفُوعُ⁩ newsletter ⁧نَشْرَةٌ بَرِيدِيَّةٌ⁩ advertising revenue ⁧عَائِدَاتُ الإِعْلَانَاتِ⁩ dismissal · dismissal ⁧سَرَّحَ⁩ · ⁧تَسْرِيح⁩ close (a newspaper) ⁧تَوَقَّفَ عَنِ الصُّدُورِ⁩ · ⁧أَغْلَقَ⁩ English Arabic freedom of the press ⁧حُرِّيَّةُ الصَّحَافَةِ⁩ ⁧تَوَقَّفَ عَنِ الصُّدُورِ⁩ The following publications have ceased to exist: ⁧الصُّدُور⁩ is the output of a newspaper ( ⁧صَدَرَ⁩ "Out, out" means: ⁧صَدَرَ العَدَدُ الأَوَّلُ⁩ The first number is out. 4. Pronunciation The foreign words. Many media terms are adapted by English or French: ⁧فِيدْيُو⁩ , ⁧بُودْكَاسْت⁩ , ⁧إِنْتَرْنِت⁩ , ⁧إِلِكْتُرُونِيّ⁩ , ⁧دِيجِيتَال⁩ (next to ⁧رَقْمِيّ⁩ ). They pronounce Arabic: full vowels, no p o v in the most traditional pronunciation ( ⁧بُودْكَاسْت⁩ may playbūdkāst•), emphasis on the penultimate heavy syllable. Listen to the tutor's pronunciation and repeat: the pronunciation "English" sounds foreign. 5. Dialogue 2 · The influencer At the house of Šarīf. Yāsmīn Show Luca a video on the phone. Arabic Translation ⁧شَاهِدْ هٰذَا المُؤَثِّرَ: لَدَيْهِ مِلْيُونَا مُتَابِعٍ، وَكُلُّ فِيدْيُو لَهُ يَنْتَشِرُ⁩ : ⁧يَاسْمِين⁩ ⁧عَلَى نِطَاقٍ وَاسِعٍ.⁩ Yāsmīn: Watch this influencer: he has two million followers, and every video of him goes viral. ⁧وَعَنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ يَتَكَلَّمُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luca: What are you talking about? ⁧عَنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ: المَطَاعِمِ، وَالسَّفَرِ، وَالأَخْبَارِ أَحْيَانًا. هٰذَا⁩ : ⁧يَاسْمِين⁩ ⁧الأُسْبُوعَ نَشَرَ مَقْطَعًا عَنْ أَزْمَةِ المِيَاهِ، فَصَارَ الوَسْمُ الأَكْثَرَ تَدَاوُلًا فِي⁩ ⁧البَلَدِ.⁩ Yāsmīn: Of everything: restaurants, travels, and sometimes news. title: Vocabulary of migration and society
text: Lesson overview Migrations, communities abroad, integration, demography and social cohesion are themes present every day in the Arab press: in the countries of origin (the remittances, the flight of doctors and engineers, the relationship with communities abroad), in transit countries and in reception countries. They are also themes where words matter: ⁧مُهَاجِر⁩ , ⁧مُغْتَرِب⁩ , ⁧لَاجِئ⁩ and ⁧نَازِح⁩ are not synonymous; "irregular" and "illegal" do not say the same; The wave and flow transform people into water. In this unit you learn the vocabulary of migration and documents, that of society (demographics, inequalities, cohesion, discrimination) and above all to choose and translate words with precision and neutrality, taking up work on connotation (B2-11) and on humanitarian vocabulary (INT-04). Three weeks, in parallel with the end of MAG-01 and with MAG-02. Item Details Code B2-20 Level B2 · Module B2.4 Variation and production Prerequisites B2-11 (connotation),04 (humanitarian lexicon: ⁧لاجئ، نازح، طالب لجوء⁩ ), B2-04 (remitted), B2-05 (documents) Estimated time 16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 233–235), plus the MAG track in separate blocks Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)70), authentic news chosen by the tutor, sessions with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. distinguish and use with precision ⁧مُهَاجِر⁩ , ⁧مُغْتَرِب⁩ , ⁧لَاجِئ⁩ , ⁧نَازِح⁩ , ⁧طَالِبُ لُجُوءٍ⁩ , ⁧جَالِيَة⁩ ; 2. understand and use the vocabulary of migration and documents (country of origin, transit, reception; residence permit, visa, reunion, naturalization, repatriation); 3. understanding and using the vocabulary of society: demography, inequalities, cohesion, discrimination; 4. to recognise the words charged and metaphors in the migration news and replace them with neutral terms; 5. to translate a short text on these subjects into two directions with precise lexicon. Three-week plan. title: Recognizing the Origin of a Speaker
text: Lesson overview Now you know the fuṣḥā, the Egyptian, the Levant (passive) and the Moroccan (passive). But the Arab world speaks of many other varieties: the Gulf, Iraq, Sudan, Tunisia, Algeria, Libya and Yemen. You can't learn all of them; But you can learn to recognize them: just a dozen words and some sounds are enough to say, most likely, this speaker comes from the Maghreb or this is an accent of the Gulf. It is a useful skill to understand (know what to expect), to translate (B2-17: The choice of variety is information) and to work with open sources. But it is also a skill to use with caution: an accent indicates a probability, not an identity. In this unit you learn the large dialect areas, a table of traits (G77), a three-step method and the correct way to report a hypothesis on variety. A new character accompanies you: Ġāda, Tunisian journalist. Three weeks, in parallel with MAG-02. Item Details Code B2-21 Level B2 · Module B2.4 Variation and production Prerequisites B2-17, B2-18; EGY and MAG tracks; B2-09 (modality and certainty) Estimated time 16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 236–238), plus the MAG track in separate blocks Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)77), authentic recordings of speakers of different varieties chosen by the tutor (interviews, public videos), sessions with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. describe the great dialectal areas of the Arab world; 2. use a table of strokes (sounds, grammar words, verb) to recognize the area of a speaker; 3. to distinguish, at least broadly, the varieties of the Maghreb and those of the Gulf and Iraq; 4. to know what factors make a hypothesis (adaptment, mobility, media, mixed varieties) uncertain; 5. refer a hypothesis on the variety with the correct degree of certainty, in English and Arabic. Three-week plan. title: Exposing and arguing by voice
text: Lesson overview In B2-10 you have learned to write an argumentative text; in B2-17 to speak a fuṣḥā natural speech; in EGY-18 to present in Egyptian educated. Now put the three things together for a central exam task B2: expose a topic for four to five minutes in front of an audience and argue in voice in a discussion, answering questions and objections. The rules change by voice: listeners cannot go back, so they need an announced structure, clear signals of passage, shorter sentences, useful repetitions, concrete examples. In this unit learn the structure of an intervention, the signals of the oral speech, the techniques to convince without manipulating, the way to handle questions and objections and to take and give up the word in a debate. Three weeks, in parallel with the end of MAG-02 and the beginning of MAG-03. Item Details Code B2-22 Level B2 · Module B2.4 Variation and production Prerequisites B2-10 (arguing texts), B2-17 (fuṣḥā ), EGY-18 (present) Estimated time 16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 239–241), plus the MAG track in separate blocks Materials This unit, a recorder (also the phone), a stopwatch, sessions with the tutor; if possible, a small audience (course partners) Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. prepare a playlist for four to five minutes without writing the complete text; 2. to open, develop and close an intervention with the signals of the oral speech; 3. use examples, data and rhetorical questions to convince, avoiding fallacies (B2-10); 4. handle questions, objections and interruptions with grace and precision; 5. to take, hold and give up the floor in a debate in fuṣḥā Talked. Pronunciation Voice, pauses and rhythm. 1) Speed: in an intervention we speak more slowly than in conversation; about 110–130 words per minute. 2) Pause: a short break after each passing signal ( ⁧أَنْتَقِلُ الآنَ إِلَى⁩ ... pause), a longer break before the final sentence. 3) Emphasis: slightly raises the voice on the keyword and slows down on numbers. 4) Fuṣḥā spoken (B2-17): desinences only where they are natural, internal vowels always correct. title: Rhetoric of public speeches
text: Lesson overview Speeches of Heads of State and Government, interventions to the United Nations and the League of Arab States, speeches for national holidays, inaugurations, election campaigns: the Arab rhetorical tradition is ancient and still alive, and a public speech in Arabic uses resources that institutional Italian uses less: parallelism, antithesis, repetition, prose rhyme, citation, titles of protocol. Knowing them serves to understand what the speech wants to achieve, to distinguish between what is promised and what is only evoked, and to translate without flattening or inflating the text. In this unit learn the main rhetorical figures and their Arabic names, protocol formulas, a method of analysis in five questions, and work on invented speeches and on a real public discourse chosen from institutional sources (Appendix C). The work is of linguistic analysis: no political judgement is required. Two weeks. Item Details Code INT-06 Level B2 · Track INT · Module B2.4 Prerequisites B2-09 (modality), B2-10 (explanation), B2-11 (connotation), B2-14 (formulas and titles), B2-22 (exhibited by voice) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 242–243), plus the MAG track Materials This unit, official speeches in Arabic published on institutional sites (Appendix C), session with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognising the parties to an official speech and the protocol formulas; 2. recognizing and naming in Arabic the main rhetorical figures (repection, parallelism, antithesis, question rhetoric, prose rhyme, quotation, metaphor, hyperbole, euphemism); 3. to distinguish in a speech the precise commitments from vague formulas, with the instruments of modality (B2-09); 4. translating a discourse by keeping the register and figures, without adding or removing emphasis; 5. write a short rhetorical analysis of a real public speech. Two-week plan. title: INT-A and INT-B exercises
text: Lesson overview This drive closes the INT track of B2 with two complete exercises, which bring together what you have learned in the four modules. INT-A is the written analysis of an article in Arabic from open sources: reading without vowels, understanding, attribution and degree of certainty, facts and opinions, signals of disinformation, translation of key steps and an analysis relationship in English with a synthesis in Arabic. INT-B is an information interview in Arabic, like that of a journalist (B2-07): preparation, questions, conduction with questions for further analysis and reformulations, verification of data and faithful report. Both have a heading; To overcome them, at least 3 on 4 in every criterion. The method is that of journalism and analysis of open sources: public texts, people who speak voluntarily in public, no operational techniques. Four weeks, while MAG closes...03. Item Details Code B2-23 Level B2 · Module B2.4 Variation and production INT trace Prerequisites INT-03 → INT-06; B2-07 → B2-14; B2-16; B2-21 Estimated time 22–24 hours · four weeks (weeks 244–247), plus the MAG track in separate blocks Materials This unit, authentic items of Arabic newspapers and institutional pages (Appendix C), a recorder, sessions with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. analyze an Arabic article without vowels 400–500 words in 90 minutes, with a six-step method; 2. write an analysis report in English (300 words) with summary, sources, degree of certainty, opinions, gaps and translated quotations; 3. write a neutral synthesis in Arabic (100 words); 4. prepare and conduct an informational interview with 15 minutes in fuṣḥā Talked, with open questions, about precision and deepening; 5. write a faithful account of the interview, distinguishing what has been said, what has not been said and what needs to be verified. Four-week plan. Dialogue 1 · 90 minutes At the police station. Nādya explains to Luke how the INT-A exercise takes place. Arabic Translation ⁧سَتَحْصُلُ عَلَى مَقَالٍ حَقِيقِيٍّ مِنْ صَحِيفَةٍ عَرَبِيَّةٍ، بِلَا تَشْكِيلٍ،⁩ : ⁧نَادْيَا⁩ ⁧فِي نَحْوِ أَرْبَعِمِئَةِ كَلِمَةٍ. وَلَدَيْكَ تِسْعُونَ دَقِيقَةً.⁩ Nādya: You will receive a true article in an Arabic newspaper, without vowels, of about four hundred words. And you have 90 minutes. ⁧لِلتَّرْجَمَةِ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ To translate it? ⁧لَا، لِلتَّحْلِيلِ. التَّرْجَمَةُ جُزْءٌ صَغِيرٌ: الفِقْرَاتُ الأَسَاسِيَّةُ فَقَطْ.⁩ : ⁧نَادْيَا⁩ ⁧المَطْلُوبُ تَقْرِيرٌ تَحْلِيلِيٌّ: مَاذَا يَقُولُ المَقَالُ، وَمَنْ يَقُولُ مَاذَا، وَبِأَيِّ⁩ ⁧دَرَجَةٍ مِنَ اليَقِينِ، وَمَا الَّذِي لَا يَقُولُهُ.⁩ Nādya: No, to analyze it. An analysis report is asked: what does the article say, who says what, with what degree of certainty, and what does not say. . ⁧لِلْخُطَبِ⁩ « ⁧الأَسْئِلَةِ الخَمْسَةِ⁩ » ⁧كَمَا فَعَلْنَا فِي⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luke: As we did with the five questions for speeches. ⁧بِالضَّبْطِ، لٰكِنْ مَعَ المَصَادِرِ. كُلُّ مَعْلُومَةٍ فِي تَقْرِيرِكَ يَجِبُ أَنْ⁩ : ⁧نَادْيَا⁩ ⁧لَمْ⁩ » ⁧،⁩ «… ⁧يَزْعُمُ حِزْبُ⁩ » ⁧،⁩ «… ⁧بِحَسَبِ وِزَارَةِ⁩ » ⁧تُنْسَبَ إِلَى مَصْدَرِهَا:⁩ ⁧وَإِذَا لَمْ يَذْكُرِ المَقَالُ مَصْدَرًا، تَكْتُبُ ذٰلِكَ.⁩ .«… ⁧يُؤَكِّدْ⁩ Nādya: Exactly, but with sources. What to notice. ⁧المَطْلُوب⁩ • what is being asked. ⁧تَقْرِيرٌ تَحْلِيلِيٌّ⁩ The test report shall be presented in the form of an analytical report. ⁧دَرَجَةُ اليَقِينِ⁩ The degree of certainty (B2-21). ⁧تُنْسَبَ إِلَى⁩ () be assigned to (B2-08). ⁧مَجْهُول⁩ "Anonymous, unknown" ⁧تَأْكِيدٌ مِنْ مَصْدَرٍ ثَانٍ⁩ • confirmation from a second source • confirmation from a second source. ⁧تَقْيِيمٌ مَنْهَجِيٌّ⁩ Methodical evaluation. ⁧إِنْ أَمْكَنَ⁩ If possible, it shall be done in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation. ⁧الصَّادِق⁩ It's honest, it's true. 2. INT-A task and address book The task. An authentic or realistic Arabic article (400–500 words, without vowels). In 90 minutes, with the dictionary only: 1) timed reading (lens ≥ 90 words per minute); 2) analysis report in English (about 300 words, section 4); 3) translation of two key paragraphs chosen by the examiner; 4) Neutral synthesis in Arabic (approximately 100 words). Criterion 4 3 2 1 Understanding all correct facts, figures and positions an inaccurate secondary detail an error on a main fact compromised sense Attribution and certainty any information with correct source and grade an inaccurate attribution or degree multiple missing or wrong attributes sources ignored Facts, opinions, signals opinions, connotations, gaps and suspected signals identified one escaped multiple escaped elements no distinction Return (report, translation, summary) clear, neutral, well-organized some inaccuracies disordered or non-neutral Incomprehensible 3. The six stages of the analysis Phase What to do Unit 1. The thresholds (5 minutes) testata, date, author, genre, title, subtitle, first and last paragraph B2-01, B2-19 2. Reading (10 minutes) silent reading timed; Mark ambiguous words with a pencil B2-16 3. The source map (15 minutes) table: who · what he says · verb of attribution · degree of certainty B2-08, B2-09 4. Facts and opinions (10 minutes) facts with source, statements, views of the journalist, words charged, suspicious signals B2-11, B2-12INT-05 5. The gaps (5 minutes) what is missing: figures, independent sources, the voice of a part, dates INT-06 6. Writing (45 minutes) report, translation of key paragraphs, summary in Arabic, rereading B2-13, B2-14 The source map is at the heart of the analysis. An example: Source What it says Word Certainty ⁧وزارة الصحة⁩ 40 new centres within the 2027 ⁧أعلنت⁩ precise commitment ⁧نقابة الأطباء⁩ missing 3000 Doctors ⁧أكدت⁩ attributed data, not verified « ⁧مصادر مطلعة⁩ » the minister could resign ⁧رجحت⁩ anonymous entry, possibility the journalist « ⁧خطوة طال انتظارها⁩ » — opinion (positive connotation) 4. The analysis report The report is written in English, in short paragraphs with titles, in neutral tone. Recommended structure: 1. References: tested, date, author, gender. 2. Summary (3–4 lines): the main fact, who, what, when. 3. Sources and locations: for each, what it says and with what degree of certainty (from the map). 4. Opinions and connotations: where the text evaluates, with the words quoted in Arabic and translated. 5. Lacks and signals: what is missing; any misinformation signals (INT-05). 6. Language notes: ambiguous words, translation choices, variety (if there are quotes in dialect, B2-21). Useful formulas in English. According to the Ministry... • • • The Party supports, without providing evidence, that... • • • Anonymous sources quoted in the newspaper consider it likely that... · • • The article does not indicate the position of... · • • The adjective X (in Arabic ...) introduces a positive assessment. · • • It is not clear if...; the text admits two readings: ... ... .... 5. Pronunciation The final timed reading. Layer B2 asks for a silent reading of at least 90 words per minute, with a correct synthesis. Twice a week, read a new article by 350–400 words with the stopwatch and record the time and quality of the oral synthesis of one minute. title: Review, simulation and profile for skill
text: Lesson overview The last four weeks of the level serve to consolidate, measure and decide where to work. There's no new grammar. In the first week you review the vocabulary for areas and the grammatical and textual framework of B2 and reread the units; in the second, do a complete simulation of the exam , with new texts and in real conditions; in the third build your profile for skill and start working on gaps; in the fourth complete recovery and review. In the week 253 support the exam B2 (Part IV). The MAG track-04 continues in its separate blocks and closes in the week 252. Item Details Code B2-24 Level B2 · Review Prerequisites Module testing B2.1 → B2.4 exceeded; INT-A and INT-B exercises (B2-23) held Estimated time 20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 249–252 of the calendar), plus the exam in the week 253; MAG-04 continues in its separate blocks Materials All volume, Appendix B (lexic), Reference Grammar (Part VI), Error Notebook, Advance Record, Authentic Articles and Newspapers (Appendix C), a native language tutor for oral simulation and an Egyptian speaker Targets. At the end of the four weeks: 1. recognize and use vocabulary B2 of the twenty-one areas of the section 2; 2. recognize without hesitation the framework structures of the section 3 and the variety of a dialect phrase; 3. read in silence an authentic article without vowels of about 400 words at least 90 words per minute and distinguish facts, sources, opinions and degree of certainty; 4. understand an interview and a debate in fuṣḥā spoken, an Egyptian song without subtitles and write a dictation with at least the 90% correct words; 5. translate an article of about 200 words (Accessories at least 3/4) and in Arabic a simple news of about 70 words; 6. write an argumentative text of about 300 words and a neutral synthesis of about 150 words; 7. expose for five minutes a topic in fuṣḥā Talk, discuss, report a news and converse in Egyptian; 8. know your skill profile and you know which units to review before the exam. Four-week plan. Do not read sections 6–10 before the simulation: the texts are new on purpose, because the simulation measures what you can do in front of a text you have never seen. If you didn't pass the test B2.4, repeat it with the tutor within the week 250, before the simulation. 1. How to Review • Active recall. Each unit has an active recall section: cover the right column and Pick up aloud. Make the units tables that the log marks as weakest; for the vocabulary use Appendix B covering the Arabic column. • Notebook of errors. Recopy the correct errors of the four module tests and INT-A and INT-exercises. B, grouped by type (reading without vowels, attribution and certainty, connotation, translation to Italian, translation to Arabic, oral register). Read them every day of the week 249. • Authentic texts. Every day, even during the review, read an authentic article without vowels and listen ten minutes of a news or talk show (Appendix C). The texts are invented but written like the real ones. • Register. title: Telling: anecdotes, unexpected and reported speech
text: Lesson overview With Layer B2 The Egyptian track passes from the phrases of everyday life to long conversation. The first step is the story: in Egypt, telling is an art, and a well-told story (ḥikāya) has a precise rhythm, with an attack, suspense, surprise, and a listener who reacts to every joke. In this unit learn the signs of the story (fi l-awwil, wi fagʾa, the-muhimm), the times of the past that serve to tell (kunt ba-..., kunt ḥa-..., kunt lissa...), the listener's reactions (lā yā šēḫ!, ya ḫabar!) and the speech reported in Egyptian: what he said, what he asked, what he said to do. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-01, B2-02 and B2-03. Item Details Code EGY-11 Level B2 · EGY track (Egyptian Cairo) Prerequisites EGY-01 EGY-10 (Volume 4) Estimated time 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 157–165), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian conversation partner, video or story podcast in Egyptian (Appendix C) Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. tell Egyptian an episode of 2–3 minutes with a clear order and a little suspense; 2. use the time of the story: past, progressive past (kunt ba-), ḥa-), I had a. 3. react to a story like an Egyptian listener; 4. report what someone has said, asked or ordered (ʾāl inn... saʾal Law... ʾalli aʿmil…); 5. follow an authentic recorded tale and summarize it. Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). Dialogue 1 · The lost suitcase Milan, September. Yāsmīn, the sister of ŠarīfShe's been here three days for her master's degree at the Polytechnic. Dinner by ŠarīfLuca asks her how the trip went. Egyptian Transliteration Translation ⁧حمد الله على السلامة يا ياسمين!⁩ : ⁧لوكا⁩ ⁧الرحلة كانت عاملة إيه؟⁩ Lūka: ḥamdilla ʿa s-salāma ya Yasmīn! ir-riḥla kānit ʿāmla ēh? Welcome, sir. Yāsmīn! Luca: What happened? ⁧في الأول كله تمام. وصلت المطار،⁩ : ⁧ياسمين⁩ ⁧ومشيت ورا الناس لحد مكان الشنط.⁩ ⁧وقفت أستنى، والشنط بتطلع واحدة ورا⁩ … ⁧التانية⁩ Yasmīn: fi l-awwil kullu tamām. wṣilt il- maṭār, wi mšīt wara n-nās li-ḥadd makān iš-šunaṭ. wiʾift astanna, wi š- šunaṭ bitiṭlaʿ waḥda wara t-tanya… Yāsmīn: At first everything is fine. I got to the airport and followed people to the baggage pickup. I started waiting, and the bags came out one after the other... ⁧وشنطتك ما طلعتش طبعًا.⁩ : ⁧شريف⁩ Šarīf: wi šanṭitik ma-ṭilʿitš ṭabʿan. Šarīf: And yours didn't go out, of course. ⁧استنى بس! كنت لسه واقفة،⁩ : ⁧ياسمين⁩ ⁧والناس مشيت كلها، وفجأة الحزام وقف.⁩ ⁧وأنا لوحدي!⁩ Yasmīn: istanna bass! kunt lissa wāʾfa, wi n-nās mišyit kullaha, wi fagʾa il- ḥizām wiʾif. wi ana li-waḥdi! YāsmīnWait! I was still standing there, everyone was gone, and all of a sudden the tape stopped. And me alone! ⁧يا خبر! وعملتي إيه؟⁩ : ⁧لوكا⁩ Lūka: ya ḫabar! wi ʿamalti ēh? Damn it! What did you do? ⁧كنت هعيط والله. بس رحت⁩ : ⁧ياسمين⁩ ⁧مكتب الشنط الضايعة، والموظفة قالتلي⁩ ⁧إن الشنطة لسه في القاهرة!⁩ Yasmīn: kunt haʿayyaṭ wallāhi. bass ruḥt maktab iš-šunaṭ iḍ-ḍayʿa, wi l- muwaẓẓafa ʾalitli inn iš-šanṭa lissa fi l- ʾAhira! Yāsmīn: I was about to cry, I swear. But I went to the lost luggage office, and the clerk told me the suitcase was still in Cairo! ⁧لا يا شيخ!⁩ : ⁧لوكا⁩ Lūka: lā ya šēḫ! Come on! ⁧وقالتلي أملا استمارة وأستنى⁩ : ⁧ياسمين⁩ ⁧تليفون. وأنا مش فاهمة نص الكلام⁩ ⁧بالإيطالي!⁩ Yasmīn: wi ʾalitli amla stimāra w- astanna tilifōn. wi ana miš fahma nuṣṣ il-kalām bi-l-iṭāli! Yāsmīn: And he told me to fill out a form and wait for a phone call. And I didn't understand half of what he said in English! ⁧والمهم، الشنطة وصلت امبارح،⁩ : ⁧شريف⁩ ⁧والحمد لله.⁩ Šarīf: wi l-muhimm, iš-šanṭa wiṣlit imbāriḥ, wi l-ḥamdu li-llāh. Šarīf: However, the suitcase arrived yesterday, thank God. ⁧يا شريف! إنت كده بوظت القصة!⁩ : ⁧ياسمين⁩ ⁧كان لسه فيه حتة حلوة!⁩ Yasmīn: ya Šarīf! inta kida bawwaẓt il- ʾiṣṣa! kān lissa fīh ḥitta ḥilwa! Yāsmīn: Šarīf! So you ruined the story! There was still a nice piece! What to notice.ḥamdilla ʿa s-salāma it is said to those who arrive from a trip (in English: "ben arrived") answer allāh yisallimak . ismaʿ ya sīdi "Listen" (Lett. "Listen, my lord"): he opens a story, even among peers. ēh ili ḥaṣal? What happened? fi l-awwil bitiṭlaʿ waḥda wara t-tanya ... they went out one after the other (bi- + imperfect for an action in the past). Stanna bass! "Wait!": he who tells does not want to be interrupted. kunt lissa wāʾfa I was still standing there. wi fagʾa Suddenly, it's all right. ya ḫabar! Damn it! kunt haʿayyaṭ I was crying (kunt + future). ʾalitli Inn... he told me... ʾalitli amla... ♪ He told me to fill in... ♪ lā ya šēḫ! Come on, I don't believe it. bawwaẓt il-ʾiṣṣa You ruined history.bawwaẓ "Round, spoil"). ḥitta "Piece": 2. The Signs of the Story An Egyptian tale has a frame of fixed words: it is as learned as if they were the punctuation of history. Function Egyptian English open ismaʿ ya sīdi · ḥaʾullak ʿala ḥāga · il-ḥikāya Inn... Listen · I'll tell you one thing · The story is that... begin fi l-awwil · awwil ma... at the beginning · just... Moving on baʿdēn · wi baʿd kida · ʿala ṭūl then · and after · immediately the surprise wi fagʾa · wi ʾilla… and suddenly · and here it is ... time lamma... · ʾabl but... · baʿd but... wi ana... When... Before... After... cut i-muhimm · ʿašān ma-ṭawwilš ʿalēk in short · to make a short story close wi ʾāḫir ḥāga... · wi ḫilṣit il-ḥikāya · wi of kānit The- and at the end... · and history is over · and that's how it is ḥikāya gone wi ana... introduces the background: wi ana māši f š-šāriʿ, šuft... while I was walking down the street, I saw... It's more natural than a blade for current actions. wi ʾilla "And here's the surprise: wi ʾilla huwwa Šarīf! And here it was. Šarīf!». 3. The Times of the Story Form Example Value past rūḥt, šuft, ʾult Action taken: the chain of events kān + bi- + imperfect kunt bāstanna · kānit bititkallim action in progress or usual in the past: kān + participle kunt wāʾfa · kān ʿāmil been in the past or action already done: I was standing, had done it. kān + ḥa- + imperfect kunt haʿayyaṭ · kān ḥa-yimši I was going to cry, he was going to leave. I also meant to kān lysa + participle kān lissa wāṣil He had just arrived. kān lissa + mā-…š kān lissa ma-wiṣilš It had not arrived yet. Participle is central. kān ʿāmil il-wāgib "He had done the tasks" "Kunt" nāsi I forgot about it. kānit rayḥa š-šuġl It was going to work.The participle says the state in which someone was, and it is often more natural than the past. 4. React In Egypt the listener participates: a story without reactions seems to be poorly heard. Egyptian When English wi baʿdēn? · ḥaṣal ēh baʿdēn? to keep it going And then what? · and then what happened? ya ḫabar! · ya ḫabar abyaḍ! surprise (positive or neutral) Damn it! · but think! ya ḫabar Iswid! Negative surprise What a disaster! lā ya šēḫ! · bi-gadd? disbelief Come on! - Really? maʿʾūla! Strong disbelief That's not possible! ʿašān Kida! understand why That's why! maʿlēš · alf salāma Consular patience · (to those who have been hurt) good wishes for prompt recovery ḥamdilla ʿa s-salāma to those who have arrived or have overcome a danger Well arrived · thank goodness that you are well The tone. ya ḫabar! it stretches (ya ḫabaaar!) and descends; bi-gadd? rises as a real question; lā ya šēḫ! It's almost a laugh. 5. Dialogue 2 · What the chief said A week later. Šarīf Go home from work and tell Luca about a meeting with his boss. Egyptian Transliteration Translation ⁧مالك؟ شكلك مضايق.⁩ : ⁧لوكا⁩ Lūka: mālak? šaklak mitḍāyiʾ. What's wrong? You look annoyed. ⁧المدير ندهني النهارده الصبح،⁩ : ⁧شريف⁩ ⁧وقالي إن المشروع اتأجل شهرين.⁩ Šarīf: il-mudīr nadahni n-naharda ṣ- ṣubḥ, wi ʾalli inn il-mašrūʿ itʾaggil šahrēn. The speech reported What it refers to Egyptian English a statement ʾāl In... · ʾalli In... · ʾalitli Inn... He said... he told me that... a yes/no application saʾalni Law (iza)... He asked me if... an open question saʾalni ana fēn · saʾalitni ʿāyiz ēh asked me where I was · what I wanted an order ʾalli aʿmil… · ʾalli arūḥ… He told me to... · go... a ban ʾalli ma-tiʿmilš… · ʾalli ma-aʿmilš… He told me not to... one entry biyʾūlu In... · sāmiʿ In... · fīh kalām Inn... They say... I heard that... No timing. In Egyptian the verb reported remains as it was: ʾalli inn iš-šanṭa lissa fi l-ʾAhira "He told me that the suitcase was still in Cairo" (Lett. It's still in the air. In Italian we make the concordance. The order reported. After ʾāl or ʾalli + person, the verb goes to the imperfect without bi-: ʾalli astana ʾalha tīgi bukra łle said to come tomorrow. The forms of ʾāl + there. ʾalli (to me) · ʾallak · ʾallik (a te m./f.) · ʾallu (to him) · ʾalha (to you) · ʾallina (to us) · ʾallukum (to you) · ʾalluhum (to them). With other subjects: ʾultillu I told him, ʾalitli "She said to me, ʾalūli They told me. 7. In a report,biyʾūlu» e « ⁧يُقَالُ⁩ (INT-01). 8. Listening to an Authentic Story What to choose. Personal stories recorded in Egyptian: short videos in which someone tells an episode (a trip, a job interview, a bad figure), conversation podcasts, interviews in which the guest remembers his own story. Choose recordings of 3–5 minutes, better with Arabic subtitles. See Appendix C. The method for a story. 1. Listen to everything once. Who tells, what happened to him, how does it end? Write three words. 2. Find the bones. Listen to and mark the signs of the story (section 2): where does the surprise begin? where Cut? 3. Find the voices. It marks every time the person who tells reports another's words (ʾalli, ʾultillu, saʾalni): who says What? 4. Tell it again. title: News: comment on the news and follow a talk show
text: Lesson overview Egyptians talk about current affairs everywhere: at coffee, in taxi, in the family, on social media. And in the TV talk shows, which are among the most followed programs in the Arab world, the conductor opens in fuṣḥā, the guest responds in Egyptian, and the conversation passes from one to the other also in the same sentence. In this unity you learn to speak of a news in Egyptian (what happened, what you think, what people say), to recognize the Egyptian caught up in debates, with the words of the fuṣḥā pronounced to the Egyptian (saqāfa, istismār, qānūn), to take and defend the word in a discussion and to distinguish a news from a voice (išāʿa) when it circulates on social media. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-03, B2-04 and B2-05. Item Details Code EGY-12 Level B2 · EGY track (Egyptian Cairo) Prerequisites EGY-11 Estimated time 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 166–174), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner, extracts of talk shows or current Egyptian programs (Appendix C) Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. report and comment on news in Egyptian, distinguishing facts, opinions and voices; 2. recognizing the words of fuṣḥā in the Egyptian pronunciation read ( ⁧ث⁩ → s, ⁧ذ⁩ → z, ⁧ق⁩ → q in translated words); 3. follow a short extract of talk show where fuṣḥā and Egyptians alternate; 4. take the floor, politely interrupt and defend its position in a debate; 5. ask and verify the source of news circulating on social media. Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). title: Practical problems: complaining, negotiating, convincing
text: Lesson overview In Egyptian practice, almost everything is negotiated: the price of a repair, a deadline for work, a favor. And it negotiates with a precise art, made of courtesy, jokes, insistence and formulas that allow everyone to come out with their heads high. In this unit you learn to file a complaint (with politeness or firmness), to bargain a price, to convince someone and to find a compromise (ḥall wasaṭ). The contexts are those of everyday life: a late plumber, a working deadline, a service that does not work. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-05, B2-06INT-03, the Test B2.1 and the beginning of B2-07. Item Details Code EGY-13 Level B2 · EGY track (Egyptian Cairo) Prerequisites EGY-12 Estimated time 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 175–183), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner, authentic videos of everyday life (Appendix C) Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. lodge a complaint in Egyptian, choosing the tone (courtesy, firm, firm) suitable for the situation; 2. contract a price or service with the typical formulas; 3. convincing someone with arguments, guarantees and a little humor; 4. propose, discuss and accept a compromise; 5. understand an authentic negotiation conversation and summarize its outcome. Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). title: Interviews: open questions, in-depth analysis, long answers
text: Lesson overview In parallel with B2-07, Egyptian track goes to the interview. In Egypt street interviews (raʾy iš-šāriʿ), the podcasts and programs in which the guest tells his life are a very popular genre, and they are also an excellent listening material: short questions, long answers, very spontaneous Egyptian. In this unit you learn to do an interview in Egyptian (open questions, requests for examples and clarifications, active listening) and to answer in a long and orderly way, to refuse with polite personal question and to follow an authentic interview. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-07, B2-08 and B2-09. Item Details Code EGY-14 Level B2 · EGY track (Egyptian Cairo) Prerequisites EGY-11 EGY-13 Estimated time 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 184–192), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner, interviews and podcasts in Egyptian (Appendix C) Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. ask open questions and in-depth questions in Egyptian (iḥkīli, zayy ēh?, ʾaṣdak ēh?); 2. to listen actively, with typical reactions and rewordings; 3. give a long and tidy answer (awwil ḥāga…, il-ḫulāṣa…); 4. to avoid too much personal demand with grace; 5. follow an authentic interview and summarize the main answers. Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). title: Humorism, proverbs and idiomatic expressions
text: Lesson overview Egyptians are famous in the Arab world for their humor: the ready joke (il-ʾafša), the self-irony, the play of words, the proverb quoted at the right time. Understanding humor is one of the last steps to truly understand a language, and also one of the most useful: in conversations, shows, social media and even talk shows, irony is everywhere. In this unity learn the vocabulary of humor (dammu ḫafīf, nukta, ʾafša), a choice of very used proverbs and frequent idiomatic expressions (fi l-mišmiš, kalām fi l-hawa, ʾalbi ʾayilli), the way to react to a joke and some rules about when and with whom to joke. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-10, B2-11 and B2-12. Item Details Code EGY-15 Level B2 · EGY track (Egyptian Cairo) Prerequisites EGY-14 Estimated time 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 193–201), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner, comedy and Egyptian humorous videos (Appendix C) Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. understanding and using the vocabulary of humor (dammu ḫafīf / tʾīl, nukta, ʾafša, biyitrayyaʾ); 2. recognize and use a dozen frequent Egyptian proverbs, with their sense; 3. understanding and using common idiomatic expressions of conversation; 4. react to a joke and respond to a friendly mockery; 5. to understand when humor is suitable and when not. Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). It is the exchange of quick lines, an Egyptian tradition: one throws an ironic phrase, the other immediately responds with another, playing on words. It is not a matter of offending but of showing readiness: those who remain unanswered laugh first. 3. Šarīf ḥayṣaḥḥa Badri? f l-mišmiš! «Šarīf Will he wake up soon? Campa cavallo! 5. Pronunciation The rhythm of the line. An Egyptian joke has a break before closing: wāḥid rāḥ il-maṭʿam... wi ʾāl li-l- garsōn... (break) .... The voice rises before the pause and then suddenly descends on the ʾafla. Dammu. The m is double (dámmu): his blood is equal. With only one m (damu) you can't understand. 6. The Proverbs Proverb literally. Sense ʿala ʾadd liḥāfak midd riglēk Spread your legs according to the blanket live by your means il-ʾirš il-abyaḍ yinfaʿ f l-yōm il-iswid the white money serves on the black day save for difficult times ili fāt māt What's past is dead. past water il-ʾird f ʿēn ummu ġazāl the monkey in the mother's eyes is a gazelle Every cockroach is beautiful to his mom il-bāb ili yigīlak minnu r-rīḥ suddu w- istirīḥ the door from which the wind comes, close it and rest avoid what causes you trouble il-ḥaraka baraka movement is blessing Moving gets something ili ma-yiʿrafš yiʾūl ʿads who doesn't know says "Lentils" He who does not know the facts judges to disprove ʾalu li-l-ḥarāmi iḥlif, ʾāl gāli l-farag And they said to the thief, Swear! He said, "Here is salvation! ask those who lie to guarantee themselves ḥabībak yiblaʿlak iẓ-ẓalaṭ, wi ʿadūwak yitamannālak il-ġalaṭ Whoever loves you swallows stones, the enemy wishes you error He who loves you forgives you all il-ʿaʾl zīna reason is an ornament It is wise to be wise. Use a proverb. An Egyptian proverb is not quoted as a curiosity: it fits into the conversation to close a speech, advise, console. After a proverb, you often add zayy but biyʾūlu As it is said to be: biyʾūl... the proverb says... The lentil proverb (illi) ma-yiʿrafš yiʾūl ʿads) is the analyst's proverb: those who do not know complete history judge badly. It's said to whom he's drawing hasty conclusions. 8. When to joke and listen to authentic humor The unwritten rules. With friends, humor is continuous, even pungent. With older people or people you don't know, wait till they're the first to joke. You are happy to joke about yourself, about traffic, about heat, about football; avoid joking about religion, the family of others and political issues with those you don't know. A joke that offends someone is not hazār: è tarʾīʾa. What to listen to. Egyptian comedies (films and series), sketches and comic monologues, humorous social videos. Many jokes play on two-way words or references to famous films: don't worry about understanding them all. See Appendix C. The method for a comedy scene. 1. The situation. Who, where, what problem? What makes the situation comical? 2. The joke. Listen again and transcribe the joke that makes you laugh (ifēh). What he plays on: words, situation, character? 3. The reaction. How do other characters react? 4. Explain it. Explain the Egyptian joke to the tutor (il-ifēh hina inn...), then in English. If a joke needs to be explained, It's not funny anymore, but you learn a lot. 9. title: Writing in Egyptian: messages, wishes and condolences
text: Lesson overview While ARZ units teach you to read the written dialect, this unity teaches you to write it: a message to a friend, an invitation, a voice message, and above all formulas for occasions (birthdays, marriages, births, outdated examinations, diseases, mourning, religious holidays), which in Egypt are almost mandatory and always have a fixed response. Wronging a formula is not serious, but knowing them well is a sign of respect that Egyptians notice and appreciate. You will also learn to choose the log (Egyptian or fuṣḥā simple) according to the recipient. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-12INT-04INT-05, the Test B2.2 and the beginning of B2-13. Item Details Code EGY-16 Level B2 · EGY track (Egyptian Cairo) Prerequisites EGY-11 EGY-15; ARZ-01 (ARZ-02 in parallel) Estimated time 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 202–210), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner, an Arabic keyboard on your phone or computer Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. write in Arabic characters a clear and consistent Egyptian message in the graphs; 2. use formulas for happy occasions and their answers; 3. tactfully write a message of closeness for an illness or mourning; 4. choose between Egyptian and fuṣḥā simple according to the recipient and the situation; 5. record and understand a voice message in Egyptian. Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). Voice messages Voice messages in Egypt ( ⁧فويس⁩ · voice) are often more frequent than written ones, even among colleagues. A good voice message: begins with a greeting and the name; state the reason immediately; not more than one minute; closes with a formula (sallim li..., mistanni raddak). Understand a vowel. It is spontaneous spoken: breaks, laughter, noises, changes of theme. The method: 1) listen to everything to understand who, why and what he asks you; 2) listens and records dates, times, places; 3) answer in writing by taking the data (ʿašān atʾakkid: il-ḥadd is-sāʿa Sit down, ṣaḥḥ?). 9. title: The Egyptian media: podcasts, documentaries, transcription and subtitles
text: Lesson overview The talk of the media is the richest source of authentic Egyptian: podcasts, documentaries, long interviews, popular videos. Compared to the dialogues of the course is faster, more disordered (pauses, repetitions, self-corrections, sentences left in half) and more mixed: English words in the podcasts of young people, fuṣḥā in the voice of the narrator and in the vocabulary of experts. In this unit learn the discursive signals that organize a story or reasoning, the rapid forms of quick speech, the conventions to transcribe the Egyptian into Arabic characters and the techniques to translate it into English, both in an integral translation and in subtitles. It's the Egyptian side of the translation form. Eight weeks, in parallel with the end of B2-13, B2-14 and B2-15. Item Details Code EGY-17 Level B2 · EGY track (Egyptian Cairo) Prerequisites EGY-11 EGY-16 (in particular EGY-14, interviews, and EGY-16, the graphs); B2-13 in parallel Estimated time 12–13 hours · eight weeks (weeks) 211–218), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, an Egyptian tutor, podcasts and authentic Egyptian videos chosen by the tutor, a program to slow down audio Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. follow 10–15 minutes of a podcast or an interview in Egyptian, understanding the main points and details important; 2. recognize the discursive signals of the story and reasoning and their function; 3. understand the most frequent rapid forms of fast speech and adapted English words; 4. transcribe into Arabic characters one minute of Egyptian, faithful version and clean version; 5. translate the Egyptian spoken in English, in full version and in subtitles. Eight-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). title: The educated Egyptian: present, discuss, converse
text: Lesson overview In EGY-17 you have learned to recognize the educated Egyptian: the Egyptian grammar with the vocabulary of fuṣḥā, who use educated people when talking about work, society or current affairs. In this unit learn how to use it: present a topic in three-five minutes, discuss and disagree nicely at a meeting, answer audience questions, hold a free conversation of 15 minutes. You also learn to switch from one register to another: the same Šarīf that in a podcast would saylaʾ w-ēh- In a meeting says "zayy" but ḥaḍratkum šayfīn». It is the last unit of the Egyptian track of B2: In the end you find the Egyptian skills profile to be checked with the tutor. Eight weeks, in parallel with the end of B2-15, B2-16, the Test B2.3 and B2-17. Item Details Code EGY-18 Level B2 · EGY track (Egyptian Cairo) Prerequisites EGY-11 EGY-17 (in particular EGY-12, talk show, and EGY-17, the educated Egyptian) Estimated time 12–13 hours · eight weeks (weeks) 219–226), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, an Egyptian tutor, a recorder (also the phone), interviews and authentic Egyptian conferences chosen by the tutor Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. reword in Egyptian read a content said in Egyptian daily; 2. submit an argument in three to five minutes with a clear structure and the appropriate formulas; 3. expressing agreement, reservations and disagreement with politeness, addressing those who listen to ḥaḍritak, ḥaḍratkum; 4. answer public questions and close an intervention; 5. support a 15-minute free conversation, using strategies not to block you. Eight-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). title: Arabic: Read Arabic in Latin characters
text: Lesson overview In the messages, comments and posts, millions of people write dialect with Latin letters and figures:3amel eh?.......................................7abibis. It is Arabic ( ⁧عَرَبِيزِي⁩ , born with the first mobile phones without Arabic keyboard and remained alive especially among young people, in Egypt, the Levant, the Gulf and the Maghreb. For those working on open sources is a frequent obstacle: a comment in Arabic is not found looking in Arabic characters, and a figure can be a letter. In this unit learn the code (what they mean 2, 3, 5, 7...), the main regional variants, the most common abbreviations and the method to transcribe a message into Arabic in Arabic characters and understand it. Unity is of understanding: it does not ask you to write in Arabic, but to read it. Five weeks, in parallel with B2-11, B2-12 and INT-04. Item Details Code ARZ-01 Level B2 · Path of variety (Arabic) Prerequisites EGY-01 EGY-14 (Egyptian); B2-11 Estimated time 7–8 hours · five weeks (weeks 199–203), about 1,5 hours per week Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner for reading aloud Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. read the Arabic letters figures and combinations and link them to the Arabic letters; 2. transcribe a short message into Egyptian Arabic characters and translate it; 3. recognize the main Levantine, Gulf and Maghrebine variants; 4. understand the most common abbreviations, English and French words and emojis; 5. avoid typical reading errors (exchanged figures, ambiguous vowels, foreign words). Five-week plan (a block from 60 minutes and one by 30 per week). title: The dialect written on social media
text: Lesson overview Today most of the written dialect no longer uses Arabic, but Arabic characters: posts, comments, captions, transcribed voice messages. The dialect in Arabic does not have an official spelling: everyone writes as pronunciation, with different graphs for the same word, elongated letters, forgotten hamza, fuṣḥā and Egyptian mixed in the same sentence. For those who work on open sources it is a valuable material (that's where you read people's reactions) and difficult (search engines don't recognize variants). In this unit learn the graphic conventions of the written Egyptian, the spy-words of the Levant and the Gulf on social media, the language of comments (irony, emoji, hashtag) and a method to read a thread separating news, opinions and vowels. Unit of Understanding . Five weeks, in parallel with INT-04INT-05 and the Test B2.2. Item Details Code ARZ-02 Level B2 · Path of variety (written dialect) Prerequisites ARZ-01; EGY-11 EGY-15; B2-12; INT-05 (in parallel) Estimated time 7–8 hours · five weeks (weeks 204–208), about 1,5 hours per week Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. recognize the most frequent Egyptian spells written in Arabic characters and link them to pronunciation; 2. recognize the spy words of the Levant and the Gulf in the comments; 3. understand the language of comments: stretches, emoji, hashtag, irony, switching with the fuṣḥā; 4. read a thread of comments and classify their content (news, opinion, voice, joke); 5. summarize in English, with the powers, the reactions of social media to a news. Five-week plan (a block from 60 minutes and one by 30 per week). title: Arrival in Fès: sounds, greetings and verb of the Moroccan
text: Lesson overview The summer of the fifth year Luke passed it to Fès, guest of the family of Karīm al-ʿAlawīThe Commission has already made a number of proposals. This is the opportunity to meet the darija , Arabic spoken in Morocco: the most distant variety from fuṣḥā among those you have encountered, because it reduces many vowels, has loans from Berber (amazigh), French and Spanish, and uses verbal forms that do not exist in Egyptian and Levantine. The MAG track is only understandable: you don't have to speak Moroccan, but understand it enough to follow a simple conversation, recognize the main traits and respond with the courtesy formulas. In this first unit learn sounds, pronouns, possession with dyal, the verb (ka-, n-, ġadi) and denial, with the formulas to greet, thank and stay at the table. Seven weeks, in parallel with B2-18, B2-19 and the beginning of B2-20. Item Details Code MAG-01 Level B2 · Track MAG (Moroccan, only understanding) Prerequisites EGY track completed; B2-17 and B2-18 (commutation, passive Levantine) Estimated time 9–10 hours · seven weeks (weeks 227–233), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a Moroccan speaker for scripts (tutor or tandem partner), video and Moroccan audio chosen by the tutor Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. recognize the darija and distinguish it from the Egyptian, the Levantine and the fuṣḥā; 2. understanding the typical sounds: reduced vowels, ǧ → ž, ṯ → t, ḏ → d; 3. understand pronouns, possession with dyals and suffixes; 4. understand the verb: present with ka-, the n- of the first person, the future with ġadi, denial but...š and māši; 5. greeting, thanking and responding to table with Moroccan formulas. Seven-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). title: In medina: numbers, prices and foreign words
text: Lesson overview Second week in Fès. Karīm Take Luca to the medina: the market, the shops, the taxi. Here the darija shows two characteristics that surprise those who come from Egyptian or Levantine: numbers (žuž for ...two, and the prices in ryal, not in dirham) and the many French and Spanish words, sometimes even Berber (amazigh), entered into the everyday language. In this unit you learn to understand numbers, prices and quantities, expressions of bargaining, the vocabulary of city and transport, and to recognize loans. As in MAG-01, the aim is to understand: production is limited to courtesy formulas and some essential demand (šḥal? () how much? Seven weeks, in parallel with B2-20, B2-21 and the beginning of B2-22. Item Details Code MAG-02 Level B2 · Track MAG (Moroccan, only understanding) Prerequisites MAG-01 Estimated time 9–10 hours · seven weeks (weeks 234–240), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a Moroccan speaker for scripts, authentic videos of markets and trips to Morocco chosen by the tutor Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. understand Moroccan numbers from 1 a 1000, with the special features of         • two • and the tens; 2. understand the prices said in ryal and convert them to dirham; 3. follow negotiation and understand quantities and measures; 4. understanding the lexicon of medina and transport; 5. recognise loans from French, Spanish and amazigh. Seven-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). Dirham and ryal The official currency is the dirham (dərhəm, plural drahəm). But in the market, taxis and daily conversations many prices are said in ryal, a traditional unit of account: 1 dirham = 20 ryal, i.e. 1 ryal = 5 cents (santim). To convert: ryal ÷ 20 = dirham . Seller says In dirham mya ryal 5 dirham alf ryal 50 dirham alphayn ryal 100 dirham ʿəšrin alf ryal 1000 dirham How do you understand? If the number looks 20 times too high, it's in ryal. The context helps: in traditional shops and among the elderly, ryal is very frequent; Dirham is used in supermarkets and documents. In some regions you can also feel Frank or Frank for the cent. The Foreign Words Origin Moroccan Meaning French ṭomobil · š-šifur · l-kuntur · santim car · driver · taximeter · cent French l-bulis · mesaž · l-frigu · l-biru police · message · refrigerator · office French l-kar · ṭ-ṭran · l-faktura bus · train · bill, invoice Spanish simana · kuzina · sbiṭar week · kitchen · hospital Spanish ṛwida · maṭiša · kamiža wheel · tomato · shirt amazigh fəkrun · fərṭəṭṭu · šlaġəm turtle · butterfly · moustache Why so many foreign words? Morocco has been in contact for centuries with the Iberian peninsula and, in the twentieth century, under French and (northern) Spanish protectorate; amazigh, official language next to Arabic from 2011, is spoken by an important part of the population. Many Moroccans also pass to French in the same sentence (B2-17): ça va? · normal · d'accord are very frequent. Recognize a loan. If a word does not have a recognizable Arabic root, try to read it aloud "French" or "Spanish": l-biru → bureau; kuzina → cocina. 7. title: In the family: hospitality, stories and television
text: Lesson overview Third stage of the stay in Fès. Luca now lives the rhythms of home al-ʿAlawī: lunch with relatives, afternoon tea, evening television, grandparents' stories. It's time to understand the darija of conversation: the names of the family, the past of the most frequent verbs (especially give it to make it, ža "Coming" means the words of the time (ʿad "Just" is, baqi is still" is, dima is always "always," ʿmmṛ "Never before"), and the formulas of hospitality, which in Morocco have an important role: rejecting food is not simple! You will also learn to orient yourself in Moroccan television, where they live together. fuṣḥā (notes), darija (series, talk show), amazigh and french. As always in the MAG track, it's about understanding; production is limited to formulas. Seven weeks, in parallel with B2-22INT-06 and B2-23. Item Details Code MAG-03 Level B2 · Track MAG (Moroccan, only understanding) Prerequisites MAG-01, MAG-02 Estimated time 9–10 hours · seven weeks (weeks 241–247), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a Moroccan speaker for scripts, standard extracts and Moroccan programs chosen by the tutor Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. understand family names and relations of kinship in darija; 2. understanding the past of the most frequent verbs, including those weak (dar, ža, kla, mša); 3. understand adverbs and expressions of time and appearance (ʿad, baqi, dima, ʿmmṛ, mn bəʿd); 4. respond to the hospitality formulas and politely refuse; 5. follow the broad lines of a scene of a Moroccan series and distinguish television registers. Seven-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). title: The media darija and the written darija
text: Lesson overview Last unit of the Moroccan track. Luca is back in Milan, but the darija follows him: the Moroccan radio that listens online, the videos that Hind sends him, the messages of Karīm, advertising and signs in holiday photos. In this unit you learn to understand the darija of the media (radio broadcasts with online listeners, advertising, videos) and especially the written darija, which meets in two forms: Arabic characters (advertising, social networks, some sites) and Latin characters with figures, such as Egyptian Arabic (ARZ-01, ARZ-02) but with own habits, influenced by French. You also learn how to orient yourself in multilingual signs (Arabic, Amazigh, French). Finally find the profile of the MAG track. Five weeks, in parallel with the Test B2.4 and B2-24. Item Details Code MAG-04 Level B2 · Track MAG (Moroccan, only understanding) Prerequisites MAG-01 MAG-03; ARZ-01, ARZ-02 (Egyptian Arabic) Estimated time 7–8 hours · five weeks (weeks 248–252), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a Moroccan speaker for scripts, radio broadcasts and Moroccan public videos chosen by the tutor Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. follow broad lines a radio broadcast in darija with speeches by the listeners; 2. read short texts in darija in Arabic characters (advertising, messages, posts); 3. read darija messages in Latin characters with digits, and their conventions to the French version of the text; 4. recognizing the languages of Moroccan cartels (Arabic, Amazigh, French); 5. evaluate your understanding profile of the Moroccan at the end B2. Five-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). The languages of the cartels In Morocco Arabic and amazigh are the official languages (the amazigh from 2011); French is widely used in administration, economy and higher education; In the north you can also hear Spanish. On official signs you often find three scriptures: Writing How to recognize it Example Arabic Arabic alphabet, from right to left ⁧وِلَايَة⁩ · ⁧مُسْتَشْفَى⁩ · ⁧مَدْرَسَة⁩ amazigh alphabet tifinagh: geometric signs (circles, crosses, lines, points), from left to right the name of the institution in amazigh French Latin alphabet École · Hôpital · Wilaya You don't need to read the tifinagh at this level: just recognize it and know that it is the official writing of the amazigh. The names of the places can appear in three different forms (e.g. the Arabic name of a city, the Amazigh and the French). 7.
